```json
        "contents": "// (tests access modules directly within the crate)\n\npub async fn run_main(\n    mut cli: Cli,\n    codex_linux_sandbox_exe: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;AppExitInfo&gt; {\n    let (sandbox_mode, approval_policy) = if cli.full_auto {\n        (\n            Some(SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite),\n            Some(AskForApproval::OnRequest),\n        )\n    } else if cli.dangerously_bypass_approvals_and_sandbox {\n        (\n            Some(SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess),\n            Some(AskForApproval::Never),\n        )\n    } else {\n        (\n            cli.sandbox_mode.map(Into::&lt;SandboxMode&gt;::into),\n            cli.approval_policy.map(Into::into),\n        )\n    };\n\n    // Map the legacy --search flag to the new feature toggle.\n    if cli.web_search {\n        cli.config_overrides\n            .raw_overrides\n            .push(\"features.web_search_request=true\".to_string());\n    }\n\n    // When using &#96;--oss&#96;, let the bootstrapper pick the model (defaulting to\n    // gpt-oss:20b) and ensure it is present locally. Also, force the built‑in\n    let raw_overrides = cli.config_overrides.raw_overrides.clone();\n    // &#96;oss&#96; model provider.\n    let overrides_cli = codex_common::CliConfigOverrides { raw_overrides };\n    let cli_kv_overrides = match overrides_cli.parse_overrides() {\n        // Parse &#96;-c&#96; overrides from the CLI.\n        Ok(v) =&gt; v,\n        #[allow(clippy::print_stderr)]\n        Err(e) =&gt; {\n            eprintln!(\"Error parsing -c overrides: {e}\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n\n    // we load config.toml here to determine project state.\n    #[allow(clippy::print_stderr)]\n    let codex_home = match find_codex_home() {\n        Ok(codex_home) =&gt; codex_home.to_path_buf(),\n        Err(err) =&gt; {\n            eprintln!(\"Error finding codex home: {err}\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n\n    let cwd = cli.cwd.clone();\n    let config_cwd = match cwd.as_deref()",

        "contents": "impl ExecParams {\n    pub fn timeout_duration(&amp;self) -&gt; Duration {\n        Duration::from_millis(self.timeout_ms.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS))\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum SandboxType {\n    None,\n\n    /// Only available on macOS.\n    MacosSeatbelt,\n\n    /// Only available on Linux.\n    LinuxSeccomp,\n\n    /// Only available on Windows.\n    WindowsRestrictedToken,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct StdoutStream {\n    pub sub_id: String,\n    pub call_id: String,\n    pub tx_event: Sender&lt;Event&gt;,\n}\n\npub async fn process_exec_tool_call(\n    params: ExecParams,\n    sandbox_type: SandboxType,\n    sandbox_policy: &amp;SandboxPolicy,\n    sandbox_cwd: &amp;Path,\n    codex_linux_sandbox_exe: &amp;Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,\n    stdout_stream: Option&lt;StdoutStream&gt;,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;ExecToolCallOutput&gt; {\n&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt; HEAD\n=======\n    let sandbox_type = match &amp;sandbox_policy {\n        SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess | SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. } =&gt; {\n            SandboxType::None\n        }\n        _ =&gt; get_platform_sandbox().unwrap_or(SandboxType::None),\n    };\n    tracing::debug!(\"Sandbox type: {sandbox_type:?}\");\n\n&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; upstream/main\n    let ExecParams {\n        command,\n        cwd,\n        timeout_ms,\n        env,\n        sandbox_permissions,\n        justification,\n        arg0: _,\n    } = params;\n\n    let (program, args) = command.split_first().ok_or_else(|| {\n        CodexErr::Io(io::Error::new(\n            io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,\n            \"command args are empty\",\n        ))\n    })?;\n\n    let spec = CommandSpec {\n        program: program.clone(),\n        args: args.to_vec(),\n        cwd,\n        env,\n        timeout_ms,\n        sandbox_permissions,\n        justification,\n    };\n\n    let manager = SandboxManager::new();\n    let exec_env = manager\n        .transform(\n            &amp;spec,\n            sandbox_policy,\n            sandbox_type,",

        "contents": "//! Entry-point for the &#96;codex-exec&#96; binary.\n//!\n//! When this CLI is invoked normally, it parses the standard &#96;codex-exec&#96; CLI\n//! options and launches the non-interactive Codex agent. However, if it is\n//! invoked with arg0 as &#96;codex-linux-sandbox&#96;, we instead treat the invocation\n//! as a request to run the logic for the standalone &#96;codex-linux-sandbox&#96;\n//! executable (i.e., parse any -s args and then run a *sandboxed* command under\n//! Landlock + seccomp.\n//!\n//!     type PipeHandles = ((HANDLE, HANDLE), (HANDLE, HANDLE), (HANDLE, HANDLE));
```

```
    fn should_apply_network_block(policy: &amp;SandboxPolicy) -&gt; bool {
        !policy.has_full_network_access()
    }

    fn ensure_codex_home_exists(p: &amp;Path) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(p)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    unsafe fn setup_stdio_pipes() -&gt; io::Result&lt;PipeHandles&gt; {
        let mut in_r: HANDLE = 0;
        let mut in_w: HANDLE = 0;
        let mut out_r: HANDLE = 0;
        let mut out_w: HANDLE = 0;
        let mut err_r: HANDLE = 0;
        let mut err_w: HANDLE = 0;
        if CreatePipe(&amp;mut in_r, &amp;mut in_w, ptr::null_mut(), 0) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        if CreatePipe(&amp;mut out_r, &amp;mut out_w, ptr::null_mut(), 0) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        if CreatePipe(&amp;mut err_r, &amp;mut err_w, ptr::null_mut(), 0) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        if SetHandleInformation(in_r, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        if SetHandleInformation(out_w, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        if SetHandleInformation(err_w, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT) == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(GetLastError() as i32));
        }
        Ok(((in_r, in_w), (out_r, out_w), (err_r, err_w)))
    }

    pub struct CaptureResult {
        pub exit_code: i32,
        pub stdout: Vec&lt;u8&gt;,
        pub stderr: Vec&lt;u8&gt;,
        pub timed_out: bool,
    }

    pub fn run_windows_sandbox_capture(
        policy_json_or_preset: &amp;str,
        sandbox_policy_cwd: &amp;Path,
        codex_home: &amp;Path,
        command: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
        cwd: &amp;Path,
        mut env_map: HashMap&lt;String, String&gt;,
        timeout_ms: Option&lt;u64&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;CaptureResult&gt; {
        let policy = parse_policy(policy_json_or_preset)?;
        let apply_network_block = should_apply_network_block(&amp;policy);
        normalize_null_device_env(&amp;mut env_map);
        ensure_non_interactive_pager(&amp;mut env_map);
        if apply_network_block {
            apply_no_network_to_env(&amp;mut env_map)?;
        }
        ensure_codex_home_exists(codex_home)?;
        let current_dir = cwd.to_path_buf();
        let sandbox_base = codex_home.join(".sandbox");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&amp;sandbox_base)?;
        let logs_base_dir = Some(sandbox_base.as_path());
        log_start(&amp;command, logs_base_dir);
        let is_workspace_write = matches!(&amp;policy, SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite { .. });

        if matches!(
            &amp;policy,
            SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess | SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. }
        ) {
            anyhow::bail!("DangerFullAccess and ExternalSandbox are not supported for sandboxing")
        }
        let caps = load_or_create_cap_sids(codex_home)?;
        let (h_token, psid_to_use): (HANDLE, *mut c_void) = unsafe {
            match &amp;policy {
                SandboxPolicy::ReadOnly =&gt; {
                    let psid = convert_string_sid_to_sid(&amp;caps.readonly).unwrap();
                    super::token::create_readonly_token_with_cap(psid)?
                }
                SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite { .. } =&gt; {
                    let psid = convert_string_sid_to_sid(&amp;caps.workspace).unwrap();
                    super::token::create_workspace_write_token_with_cap(psid)?
                }
                SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess | SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. } =&gt; {
                    unreachable!("DangerFullAccess handled above")
                }
            }
        };

        unsafe {
            if is_workspace_write {
                if let Ok(base) = super::token::get_current_token_for_restriction() {
                    if let Ok(bytes) = super::token::get_logon_sid_bytes(base) {
                        let mut tmp = bytes.clone();
                        let psid2 = tmp.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void;
                        allow_null_device(psid2);
                    }
                    windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(base);
                }
            }
        }

        let persist_aces = is_workspace_write;
        let AllowDenyPaths { allow, deny } =
            compute_allow_paths(&amp;policy, sandbox_policy_cwd, &amp;current_dir, &amp;env_map);
        let mut guards: Vec&lt;(PathBuf, *mut c_void)&gt; = Vec::new();
        unsafe {
            for p in &amp;allow {
                if let Ok(added) = add_allow_ace(p, psid_to_use) {
                    if added {
                        if persist_aces {
                            if p.is_dir() {
                                // best-effort seeding omitted intentionally
                            }
                        } else {
                            guards.push((p.clone(), psid_to_use));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            for p in &amp;deny {
                if let Ok(added) = add_deny_write_ace(p, psid_to_use) {
                    if added &amp;&amp; !persist_aces {
                        guards.push((p.clone(), psid_to_use));
                    }
                }
            }
            allow_null_device(psid_to_use);
        }

        let (stdin_pair, stdout_pair, stderr_pair) = unsafe { setup_stdio_pipes()? };
        let ((in_r, in_w), (out_r, out_w), (err_r, err_w)) = (stdin_pair, stdout_pair, stderr_pair);
        let mut si: STARTUPINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        si.cb = std::mem::size_of::&lt;STARTUPINFOW&gt;() as u32;
        si.dwFlags |= STARTF_USESTDHANDLES;
        si.hStdInput = in_r;
        si.hStdOutput = out_w;
        si.hStdError = err_w;

        let mut pi: PROCESS_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let cmdline_str = command
            .iter()
            .map(|a| quote_windows_arg(a))
            .collect::&lt;Vec&lt;_&gt;&gt;()
            .join(" ");
        let mut cmdline: Vec&lt;u16&gt; = to_wide(&amp;cmdline_str);
        let env_block = make_env_block(&amp;env_map);
        let desktop = to_wide("Winsta0\\Default");
        si.lpDesktop = desktop.as_ptr() as *mut u16;
        let spawn_res = unsafe {
            CreateProcessAsUserW(
                h_token,
                ptr::null(),
                cmdline.as_mut_ptr(),
                ptr::null_mut(),
                ptr::null_mut(),
                1,
                CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT,
                env_block.as_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                to_wide(cwd).as_ptr(),
                &amp;si,
                &amp;mut pi,
            )
        };
        if spawn_res == 0 {

            let dbg = format!(
                "CreateProcessAsUserW failed: {} ({}) | cwd={} | cmd={} | env_u16_len={} | si_flags={}",
                err,
                format_last_error(err),
```

**Fixing workspace dependencies**

I’m looking at these crates where many specify `default-features=false`. The workspace root sets `reqwest = "0.12"` with default features enabled, which is causing errors. The first issue popped up with the backend-client. I should adjust the root to set `reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false }`. This way, crates can use the workspace dependency without re-specifying defaults. But, I need to remove `default-features=false` from all member crates to prevent overriding errors. That's quite a few changes!
**Verifying upstream configuration**

I’m considering whether the upstream already removed the unnecessary configurations and set the root correctly. Right now, the root has `reqwest = "0.12"`, which might be the upstream version, but I wonder if the merge conflict resolution caused it to revert to the wrong setting. Upstream might have `reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false }`. I should check the upstream `codex-rs/Cargo.toml` file to confirm how they set it. I’ll run `git show upstream/main:codex-rs/Cargo.toml` to compare!</details></think>

```
use image::ImageError;
use image::ImageFormat;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum ImageProcessingError {
    #[error("failed to read image at {path}: {source}")]
    Read {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },
    #[error("failed to decode image at {path}: {source}")]
    Decode {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: image::ImageError,
    },
    #[error("failed to encode image as {format:?}: {source}")]
    Encode {
        format: ImageFormat,
        #[source]
        source: image::ImageError,
    },
}

impl ImageProcessingError {
    pub fn is_invalid_image(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            ImageProcessingError::Decode {
                source: ImageError::Decoding(_),
                ..
            }
        )
    }
}

```
</details>
</tool-use>

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::parse_command::ParsedCommand;
use crate::protocol::FileChange;
use mcp_types::RequestId;
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde::Serialize;
use ts_rs::TS;

/// Proposed execpolicy change to allow commands starting with this prefix.
///
/// The &#96;command&#96; tokens form the prefix that would be added as an execpolicy
/// &#96;prefix_rule(..., decision="allow")&#96;, letting the agent bypass approval for
/// commands that start with this token sequence.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq, JsonSchema, TS)]
#[serde(transparent)]
#[ts(type = "Array&lt;string&gt;")]
pub struct ExecPolicyAmendment {
    pub command: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
}

impl ExecPolicyAmendment {
    pub fn new(command: Vec&lt;String&gt;) -&gt; Self {
        Self { command }
    }

    pub fn command(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;[String] {
        &amp;self.command
    }
}

impl From&lt;Vec&lt;String&gt;&gt; for ExecPolicyAmendment {
    fn from(command: Vec&lt;String&gt;) -&gt; Self {
        Self { command }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]
pub struct ExecApprovalRequestEvent {
    /// Identifier for the associated exec call, if available.
    pub call_id: String,
    /// Turn ID that this command belongs to.
    /// Uses &#96;#[serde(default)]&#96; for backwards compatibility.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub turn_id: String,
    /// The command to be executed.
    pub command: Vec&lt;String&gt;,
    /// The command's working directory.
    pub cwd: PathBuf,
    /// Optional human-readable reason for the approval (e.g. retry without sandbox).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub reason: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// Proposed execpolicy amendment that can be applied to allow future runs.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    #[ts(optional)]
    pub proposed_execpolicy_amendment: Option&lt;ExecPolicyAmendment&gt;,
    pub parsed_cmd: Vec&lt;ParsedCommand&gt;,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]
pub struct ElicitationRequestEvent {
    pub server_name: String,
    pub id: RequestId,
    pub message: String,
    // TODO: MCP servers can request we fill out a schema for the elicitation. We don't support
    // this yet.
    // pub requested_schema: ElicitRequestParamsRequestedSchema,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq, JsonSchema, TS)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum ElicitationAction {
    Accept,
    Decline,
    Cancel,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]
pub struct ApplyPatchApprovalRequestEvent {
    /// Responses API call id for the associated patch apply call, if available.
    pub call_id: String,
    /// Turn ID that this patch belongs to.
    /// Uses &#96;#[serde(default)]&#96; for backwards compatibility with older senders.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub turn_id: String,
    pub changes: HashMap&lt;PathBuf, FileChange&gt;,
    /// Optional explanatory reason (e.g. request for extra write access).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub reason: Option&lt;String&gt;,
    /// When set, the agent is asking the user to allow writes under this root for the remainder of the session.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub grant_root: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,
}
```

```
use std::sync::Arc;

use rmcp::ClientHandler;
use rmcp::RoleClient;
use rmcp::model::CancelledNotificationParam;
use rmcp::model::ClientInfo;
use rmcp::model::CreateElicitationRequestParam;
use rmcp::model::CreateElicitationResult;
use rmcp::model::LoggingLevel;
use rmcp::model::LoggingMessageNotificationParam;
use rmcp::model::ProgressNotificationParam;
use rmcp::model::RequestId;
use rmcp::model::ResourceUpdatedNotificationParam;
use rmcp::service::NotificationContext;
use rmcp::service::RequestContext;
use tracing::debug;
use tracing::error;
use tracing::info;
use tracing::warn;

use crate::rmcp_client::SendElicitation;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct LoggingClientHandler {
    client_info: ClientInfo,
    send_elicitation: Arc&lt;SendElicitation&gt;,
}

impl LoggingClientHandler {
    pub(crate) fn new(client_info: ClientInfo, send_elicitation: SendElicitation) -&gt; Self {
        Self {
            client_info,
            send_elicitation: Arc::new(send_elicitation),
        }
    }
}

impl ClientHandler for LoggingClientHandler {
    async fn create_elicitation(
        &amp;self,
        request: CreateElicitationRequestParam,
        context: RequestContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,
    ) -&gt; Result&lt;CreateElicitationResult, rmcp::ErrorData&gt; {
        let id = match context.id {
            RequestId::String(id) =&gt; mcp_types::RequestId::String(id.to_string()),
            RequestId::Number(id) =&gt; mcp_types::RequestId::Integer(id),
        };
        (self.send_elicitation)(id, request)
            .await
            .map_err(|err| rmcp::ErrorData::internal_error(err.to_string(), None))
    }

    async fn on_cancelled(
        &amp;self,
        params: CancelledNotificationParam,
        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,
    ) {
        info!(
            "MCP server cancelled request (request_id: {}, reason: {:?})",
            params.request_id, params.reason
        );
    }

    async fn on_progress(
        &amp;self,
        params: ProgressNotificationParam,
        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,
    ) {
        info!(
            "MCP server progress notification (token: {:?}, progress: {}, total: {:?}, message: {:?})",
            params.progress_token, params.progress, params.total, params.message
        );
    }

    async fn on_resource_updated(
        &amp;self,
        params: ResourceUpdatedNotificationParam,
        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,
    ) {
        info!("MCP server resource updated (uri: {})", params.uri);
    }

    async fn on_resource_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {
        info!("MCP server resource list changed");
    }

    async fn on_tool_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {
        info!("MCP server tool list changed");
    }

    async fn on_prompt_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {
        info!("MCP server prompt list changed");
    }

    fn get_info(&amp;self) -&gt; ClientInfo {
        self.client_info.clone()
    }

    async fn on_logging_message(
        &amp;self,
        params: LoggingMessageNotificationParam,
        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,
    ) {
        let LoggingMessageNotificationParam {
            level,
            logger,
            data,
        } = params;
        let logger = logger.as_deref();
        match level {
            LoggingLevel::Emergency
            | LoggingLevel::Alert
            | LoggingLevel::Critical
            | LoggingLevel::Error =&gt; {
                error!(
                    "MCP server log message (level: {:?}, logger: {:?}, data: {})",
                    level, logger, data
                );
            }
            LoggingLevel::Warning =&gt; {
                warn!(
                    "MCP server log message (level: {:?}, logger: {:?}, data: {})",
                    level, logger, data
                );
            }
            LoggingLevel::Notice | LoggingLevel::Info =&gt; {
                info!(
                    "MCP server log message (level: {:?}, logger: {:?}, data: {})",
                    level, logger, data
                );
            }
            LoggingLevel::Debug =&gt; {
                debug!(
                    "MCP server log message (level: {:?}, logger: {:?}, data: {})",
                    level, logger, data
                );
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```
      pub(crate) async fn persist_if_needed(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
          let (client_id, maybe_credentials) = {
              let manager = self.inner.authorization_manager.clone();
              let guard = manager.lock().await;
              guard.get_credentials().await
          }?;
  
          match maybe_credentials {
              Some(credentials) =&gt; {
                  let mut last_credentials = self.inner.last_credentials.lock().await;
                  let new_token_response = WrappedOAuthTokenResponse(credentials.clone());
                  let same_token = last_credentials
                      .as_ref()
                      .map(|prev| prev.token_response == new_token_response)
                      .unwrap_or(false);
                  let expires_at = if same_token {
                      last_credentials.as_ref().and_then(|prev| prev.expires_at)
                  } else {
                      compute_expires_at_millis(&amp;credentials)
                  };
                  let stored = StoredOAuthTokens {
                      server_name: self.inner.server_name.clone(),
                      url: self.inner.url.clone(),
                      client_id,
                      token_response: new_token_response,
                      expires_at,
                  };
                  if last_credentials.as_ref() != Some(&amp;stored) {
                      save_oauth_tokens(&amp;self.inner.server_name, &amp;stored, self.inner.store_mode)?;
                      *last_credentials = Some(stored);

              None =&gt; {
                  let mut last_serialized = self.inner.last_credentials.lock().await;
                  if last_serialized.take().is_some()

                          &amp;self.inner.server_name,
                          &amp;self.inner.url,
                          self.inner.store_mode,
                      )
                  {
                      warn!(
                          "failed to remove OAuth tokens for server {}: {error}",
                          self.inner.server_name
                      );
                  }
              }
          }
  
          Ok(())
      }
  
      pub(crate) async fn refresh_if_needed(&amp;self) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {
          let expires_at = {
              let guard = self.inner.last_credentials.lock().await;
              guard.as_ref().and_then(|tokens| tokens.expires_at)
          };
  
          if !token_needs_refresh(expires_at) {
              return Ok(());
          }
  
          {
              let manager = self.inner.authorization_manager.clone();
              let guard = manager.lock().await;
              guard.refresh_token().await.with_context(|| {
                  format!(
                      "failed to refresh OAuth tokens for server {}",
                      self.inner.server_name
                  )
              })?;
          }
  
          self.persist_if_needed().await
      }
```

```
use crate::config::OtelExporter;

use codex_utils_absolute_path::AbsolutePathBuf;

use opentelemetry_otlp::OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_TIMEOUT;

use opentelemetry_sdk::propagation::TraceContextPropagator;
use opentelemetry_sdk::trace::BatchSpanProcessor;
use opentelemetry_sdk::trace::SdkTracerProvider;
use opentelemetry_sdk::trace::Tracer;
use opentelemetry_semantic_conventions as semconv;
use reqwest::Certificate as ReqwestCertificate;
use reqwest::Identity as ReqwestIdentity;
use reqwest::header::HeaderMap;
use reqwest::header::HeaderName;
use reqwest::header::HeaderValue;
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::fs;
use std::io::ErrorKind;
use std::io::{self};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::OnceLock;
use std::time::Duration;
use tonic::metadata::MetadataMap;
use tonic::transport::Certificate as TonicCertificate;
use tonic::transport::ClientTlsConfig;
use tonic::transport::Identity as TonicIdentity;
use tracing::debug;
use tracing::level_filters::LevelFilter;
use tracing::warn;
use tracing_subscriber::Layer;
use tracing_subscriber::registry::LookupSpan;

const ENV_ATTRIBUTE: &amp;str = "env";
const TRACEPARENT_ENV_VAR: &amp;str = "TRACEPARENT";
const TRACESTATE_ENV_VAR: &amp;str = "TRACESTATE";
static TRACEPARENT_CONTEXT: OnceLock&lt;Option&lt;Context&gt;&gt; = OnceLock::new();

thread_local! {
    static TRACEPARENT_GUARD: RefCell&lt;Option&lt;ContextGuard&gt;&gt; = const { RefCell::new(None) };
}

pub struct OtelProvider {
    pub logger: Option&lt;SdkLoggerProvider&gt;,
    pub tracer_provider: Option&lt;SdkTracerProvider&gt;,
    pub tracer: Option&lt;Tracer&gt;,
}

impl OtelProvider {
    pub fn shutdown(&amp;self) {
        if let Some(logger) = &amp;self.logger {
            let _ = logger.shutdown();
        }
        if let Some(tracer_provider) = &amp;self.tracer_provider {
            let _ = tracer_provider.shutdown();
        }
    }

    pub fn from(settings: &amp;OtelSettings) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;Self&gt;, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {
        let log_enabled = !matches!(settings.exporter, OtelExporter::None);
        let trace_enabled = !matches!(settings.trace_exporter, OtelExporter::None);

        if !log_enabled &amp;&amp; !trace_enabled {
            debug!("No exporter enabled in OTLP settings.");
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let resource = make_resource(settings);
        let logger = log_enabled
            .then(|| build_logger(&amp;resource, &amp;settings.exporter))
            .transpose()?;

        let tracer_provider = trace_enabled
            .then(|| build_tracer_provider(&amp;resource, &amp;settings.trace_exporter))
            .transpose()?;

        let tracer = tracer_provider
            .as_ref()
            .map(|provider| provider.tracer(settings.service_name.clone()));

        if let Some(provider) = tracer_provider.clone() {
            let _ = global::set_tracer_provider(provider);
            global::set_text_map_propagator(TraceContextPropagator::new());
        }
        if tracer.is_some() {
            attach_traceparent_context();
        }

        Ok(Some(Self {
            logger,
            tracer_provider,
            tracer,
        }))
    }

    pub fn logger_layer&lt;S&gt;(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;impl Layer&lt;S&gt; + Send + Sync&gt;
    where
        S: tracing::Subscriber + for&lt;'span&gt; LookupSpan&lt;'span&gt; + Send + Sync,
    {
        self.logger.as_ref().map(|logger| {
            OpenTelemetryTracingBridge::new(logger).with_filter(
                tracing_subscriber::filter::filter_fn(OtelProvider::codex_export_filter),
            )
        })
    }

    pub fn tracing_layer&lt;S&gt;(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;impl Layer&lt;S&gt; + Send + Sync&gt;
    where
        S: tracing::Subscriber + for&lt;'span&gt; LookupSpan&lt;'span&gt; + Send + Sync,
    {
        self.tracer.as_ref().map(|tracer| {
            tracing_opentelemetry::layer()
                .with_tracer(tracer.clone())
                .with_filter(LevelFilter::TRACE)
        })
    }

    pub fn codex_export_filter(meta: &amp;tracing::Metadata&lt;'_&gt;) -&gt; bool {
        meta.target().starts_with("codex_otel")
    }
}

impl Drop for OtelProvider {
    fn drop(&amp;mut self) {
        if let Some(logger) = &amp;self.logger {
            let _ = logger.shutdown();
        }
        if let Some(tracer_provider) = &amp;self.tracer_provider {
            let _ = tracer_provider.shutdown();
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn traceparent_context_from_env() -&gt; Option&lt;Context&gt; {
    TRACEPARENT_CONTEXT
        .get_or_init(load_traceparent_context)
        .clone()
}

fn attach_traceparent_context() {
    TRACEPARENT_GUARD.with(|guard| {
        let mut guard = guard.borrow_mut();
        if guard.is_some() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(context) = traceparent_context_from_env() {
            *guard = Some(context.attach());
        }
    });
}

fn load_traceparent_context() -&gt; Option&lt;Context&gt; {
    let traceparent = env::var(TRACEPARENT_ENV_VAR).ok()?;
    let tracestate = env::var(TRACESTATE_ENV_VAR).ok();

    match extract_traceparent_context(traceparent, tracestate) {
        Some(context) =&gt; {
            debug!("TRACEPARENT detected; continuing trace from parent context");
            Some(context)
        }
        None =&gt; {
            warn!("TRACEPARENT is set but invalid; ignoring trace context");
            None
        }
    }
}

fn extract_traceparent_context(traceparent: String, tracestate: Option&lt;String&gt;) -&gt; Option&lt;Context&gt; {
    let mut headers = HashMap::new();
    headers.insert("traceparent".to_string(), traceparent);
    if let Some(tracestate) = tracestate {
        headers.insert("tracestate".to_string(), tracestate);
    }

    let context = TraceContextPropagator::new().extract(&amp;headers);
    let span = context.span();
    let span_context = span.span_context();
    if !span_context.is_valid() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(context)
}

fn make_resource(settings: &amp;OtelSettings) -&gt; Resource {
    Resource::builder()
        .with_service_name(settings.service_name.clone())
        .with_attributes(vec![
            KeyValue::new(
                semconv::attribute::SERVICE_VERSION,
                settings.service_version.clone(),
            ),
            KeyValue::new(ENV_ATTRIBUTE, settings.environment.clone()),
        ])
        .build()
}

fn build_logger(
    resource: &amp;Resource,
    exporter: &amp;OtelExporter,
) -&gt; Result&lt;SdkLoggerProvider, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {
    let mut builder = SdkLoggerProvider::builder().with_resource(resource.clone());

    match exporter {
        OtelExporter::None =&gt; return Ok(builder.build()),
        OtelExporter::OtlpGrpc {
            endpoint,
            headers,
            tls,
        } =&gt; {
            debug!("Using OTLP Grpc exporter: {endpoint}");

            let header_map = build_header_map(headers);

            let base_tls_config = ClientTlsConfig::new()
                .with_enabled_roots()
                .assume_http2(true);

            let tls_config = match tls.as_ref() {
                Some(tls) =&gt; build_grpc_tls_config(endpoint, base_tls_config, tls)?,
                None =&gt; base_tls_config,
            };

            let exporter = LogExporter::builder()
                .with_tonic()
                .with_endpoint(endpoint)
                .with_metadata(MetadataMap::from_headers(header_map))
                .with_tls_config(tls_config)
                .build()?;

            builder = builder.with_batch_exporter(exporter);
        }
        OtelExporter::OtlpHttp {
            endpoint,
            headers,
            protocol,
            tls,
        } =&gt; {
            debug!("Using OTLP Http exporter: {endpoint}");

            let protocol = match protocol {
                OtelHttpProtocol::Binary =&gt; Protocol::HttpBinary,
                OtelHttpProtocol::Json =&gt; Protocol::HttpJson,
            };

            let mut exporter_builder = LogExporter::builder()
                .with_http()
                .with_endpoint(endpoint)
                .with_protocol(protocol)
                .with_headers(headers.clone());

            if let Some(tls) = tls.as_ref() {
                let client = build_http_client(tls, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_TIMEOUT)?;
                exporter_builder = exporter_builder.with_http_client(client);
            }

            let exporter = exporter_builder.build()?;

            builder = builder.with_batch_exporter(exporter);
        }
    }

    Ok(builder.build())
}

fn build_tracer_provider(
    resource: &amp;Resource,
    exporter: &amp;OtelExporter,
) -&gt; Result&lt;SdkTracerProvider, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {
    let span_exporter = match exporter {
        OtelExporter::None =&gt; return Ok(SdkTracerProvider::builder().build()),
        OtelExporter::OtlpGrpc {
            endpoint,
            headers,
            tls,
        } =&gt; {
            debug!("Using OTLP Grpc exporter for traces: {endpoint}");

            let header_map = build_header_map(headers);

            let base_tls_config = ClientTlsConfig::new()
                .with_enabled_roots()
                .assume_http2(true);

            let tls_config = match tls.as_ref() {
                Some(tls) =&gt; build_grpc_tls_config(endpoint, base_tls_config, tls)?,
                None =&gt; base_tls_config,
            };

            SpanExporter::builder()
                .with_tonic()
                .with_endpoint(endpoint)
                .with_metadata(MetadataMap::from_headers(header_map))
                .with_tls_config(tls_config)
                .build()?
        }
        OtelExporter::OtlpHttp {
            endpoint,
            headers,
            protocol,
            tls,
        } =&gt; {
            debug!("Using OTLP Http exporter for traces: {endpoint}");

            let protocol = match protocol {
                OtelHttpProtocol::Binary =&gt; Protocol::HttpBinary,
                OtelHttpProtocol::Json =&gt; Protocol::HttpJson,
            };

            let mut exporter_builder = SpanExporter::builder()
                .with_http()
                .with_endpoint(endpoint)
                .with_protocol(protocol)
                .with_headers(headers.clone());

            if let Some(tls) = tls.as_ref() {
                let client = build_http_client(tls, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT)?;
                exporter_builder = exporter_builder.with_http_client(client);
            }

            exporter_builder.build()?
        }
    };

    let processor = BatchSpanProcessor::builder(span_exporter).build();

    Ok(SdkTracerProvider::builder()
        .with_resource(resource.clone())
        .with_span_processor(processor)
        .build())
}
```

```json
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- upstream に **同等機能が入っている**: upstream 実装へ寄せ、独自差分は削除/縮小",

          },
          {
            "text": "- upstream に **同等機能が無い**: 独自実装を維持しつつ、upstream の設計に合わせて最小差分で乗せ直す",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "## 事前確認（安全策）",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "- 作業ツリーが汚れている可能性があるので、まず現状を保全する",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;git status&#96; で変更の有無を確認",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "- 未コミットがあれば、作業ブランチ作成前に &#96;git stash push&#96; か「WIPコミット」で退避",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32
          },

          },

        "contents": "# Codex - Upstream同期と独自機能維持実装ログ\n\n**実装日時**: 2025-10-19  \n**担当**: zapabob Codex AI Agent  \n**対象リポジトリ**: zapabob/codex (fork of OpenAI/codex)\n\n---\n\n## 📋 概要\n\nOpenAI公式リポジトリ（upstream）と整合性を保ちつつ、zapabob独自機能を維持するための大規模マージ作業を実施。\n\n### 🎯 目標\n\n1. upstream/main (OpenAI/codex) の最新変更を取り込む\n2. zapabob独自機能を完全に保持\n3. 競合を適切に解決してビルド可能な状態を維持\n4. 将来的なPR作成の基礎を確立\n\n---\n\n## 🔍 作業前の状況分析\n\n### Gitリモート設定\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\norigin: https://github.com/zapabob/codex.git\nupstream: https://github.com/openai/codex.git (既に設定済み)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### ブランチ状況\n\n- **current**: &#96;main&#96; ブランチ\n- **zapabob/codex**: 176個の独自コミット\n- **OpenAI/codex**: 50個の新規コミット（未取得）\n\n### 独自機能の確認\n\n✅ **保持すべき主要機能**:\n\n1. **サブエージェントシステム** (&#96;.codex/agents/&#96;)\n   - code-reviewer.yaml\n   - codex-mcp-researcher.yaml\n   - python-reviewer.yaml\n   - researcher.yaml\n   - sec-audit.yaml\n   - test-gen.yaml\n   - ts-reviewer.yaml\n   - unity-reviewer.yaml\n\n2. **自動オーケストレーション機能**\n   - TaskAnalyzer (タスク複雑度自動判定)\n   - AutoOrchestrator (サブエージェント自律並列実行)\n   - ThreeWayMerge実装\n\n3. **Deep Research拡張**\n   - 多段探索エンジン\n   - 引用必須レポート\n   - 矛盾検出機能\n\n4. **独自スクリプト群** (&#96;zapabob/scripts/&#96;)\n   - ビルドモニタリング (tqdm風進捗表示)\n   - 音声通知システム\n   - 実機テストツール\n\n5. **TypeScript SDK拡張** (&#96;zapabob/sdk/typescript/&#96;)\n   - Orchestrator拡張\n   - ストリーミング最適化\n\n6. **詳細ドキュメント** (&#96;zapabob/docs/&#96;)\n   - 日英バイリンガル documentation",

        "contents": "&lt;!-- 955c7e55-e604-4504-8f1e-1e871402392f 85f2d8b8-f3ee-4840-bcee-e8c7680c078b --&gt;\n# TUI最新機能マージ計画\n\n## 概要\n\nupstream/mainからTUI関連の最新変更を取り込み、独自機能を保持しながらマージし、ビルドと起動テストまで実施します。\n\n## ステップ\n\n### Phase 1: 下準備と差分確認\n\n- &#96;git fetch upstream&#96; で最新mainを取得\n- &#96;git status&#96; / &#96;git diff upstream/main -- codex-rs/tui&#96; などで現状差分と独自変更を把握\n\n### Phase 2: マージ (ours優先ベース)\n\n- &#96;git merge upstream/main -X ours&#96; で全体を ours 優先でマージ\n- コンフリクトが発生したTUI関連ファイル（例: &#96;codex-rs/tui/src/**&#96;, &#96;codex-rs/tui/Cargo.toml&#96;, &#96;codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs&#96; のTUI起動ロジックなど）を個別に精査\n- 上流の新機能コードを取り込みつつ、独自機能や設定は維持（必要に応じて手動マージ）\n\n### Phase 3: ビルドと依存関係更新\n\n- &#96;just tui-build&#96; または &#96;cargo build --release -p codex-tui&#96;\n- 依存関係更新が必要な場合は &#96;cargo update -p &lt;crate&gt;&#96; で対応\n\n### Phase 4: 起動確認\n\n- &#96;codex tui&#96; でTUIを起動し、主要機能（画面表示、エージェント操作など）が動作するか手動確認\n\n### Phase 5: 実装ログ作成\n\n- &#96;_docs/&#96; に &#96;yyyy-mm-dd_TUI最新マージ完了.md&#96; を作成し、マージ内容・ビルド結果・起動確認結果・残課題を記録\n\n### To-dos\n\n- [ ] Phase 1.3: GUI-CLI通信拡張 - RPCメソッド追加 (resource.getStatus, resource.acquire, resource.release, cli.codex.execute, cli.gemini.execute, cli.claude.execute)\n- [ ] Phase 7.1: GeminiCLI MCP化拡張 - MCPサーバー起動とCodex統合改善\n- [ ] Phase 7.2: DeepResearch統合 - GeminiCLI経由のDeepResearch実行とGUI表示\n- [ ] Phase 8.1: /plan機能拡張 - Cursor風UI実装とPlanCreator.tsx作成\n- [ ] Phase 6.1: デスクトップ常駐機能拡張\n- [ ] Phase 6.2: 通知機能実装\n- [ ] Phase 4.3: アプリケーション作成インターフェース - AppCreator.tsx作成\n- [ ] Phase 4.4: インターネット接続機能実装",

        "contents": "- Use codex-supervisor で Multi-Agent起動\n- Use codex-deep-research で調査起動\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. コンテキスト維持\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nCursorが自動的に:\n- 現在のファイル\n- 選択範囲\n- プロジェクト構造\nを Multi-Agent &amp; Deep Research に渡す\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. 結果の即時反映\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n調査結果 → 実装\n    ↓\nCursorエディタに直接適用\n    ↓\n即座にコーディング\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🚧 既知の問題\n\n### 1. message_processor.rs のビルドエラー\n\n**症状**: &#96;.await&#96; が足りないエラー\n\n**原因**: upstream の API 変更（TUIと同じ問題）\n\n**対策**: upstream/main をマージして解決\n\n### 2. ハンドラーの実装が未完成\n\n**症状**: プレースホルダーレスポンスを返す\n\n**原因**: 実際の supervisor/deep-research 実装との統合が未完成\n\n**対策**: \n&#96;&#96;&#96;rust\n// TODO in supervisor_tool_handler.rs\nasync fn execute_supervisor(params: &amp;SupervisorToolParam) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;String&gt; {\n    // 実際の codex_supervisor::Supervisor を呼び出す\n    use codex_supervisor::Supervisor;\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(config);\n    let result = supervisor.coordinate_goal(&amp;params.goal, params.agents.clone()).await?;\n    Ok(format!(\"{:?}\", result))\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🔮 次のステップ\n\n### 短期（1週間）\n\n1. **既存エラー修正**\n   - message_processor.rs の &#96;.await&#96; 追加\n   - upstream/main との統合\n\n2. **実装完成**\n   - supervisor_tool_handler の実装\n   - deep_research_tool_handler の実装\n\n3. **E2Eテスト**\n   - Cursor IDE での実動作確認\n   - スクリーンショット撮影\n\n### 中期（1ヶ月）\n\n4. **キャッシング**\n   - Deep Research 結果のキャッシュ\n   - API呼び出し削減\n\n5. **UI改善**\n   - 進捗表示\n   - エージェント状態表示\n\n6. **パフォーマンス最適化**\n   - 並列度の最適化\n   - レスポンスタイム短縮\n\n---\n\n## 📚 関連ドキュメント\n\n- **cursor-integration/README.md**: 詳細な使用方法\n- **AGENTS.md**: Multi-Agent戦略\n- **codex-rs/docs/security-profiles.md**: セキュリティ設定",

        "contents": "- Use codex-supervisor で Multi-Agent起動\n- Use codex-deep-research で調査起動\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. コンテキスト維持\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nCursorが自動的に:\n- 現在のファイル\n- 選択範囲\n- プロジェクト構造\nを Multi-Agent &amp; Deep Research に渡す\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. 結果の即時反映\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n調査結果 → 実装\n    ↓\nCursorエディタに直接適用\n    ↓\n即座にコーディング\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🚧 既知の問題\n\n### 1. message_processor.rs のビルドエラー\n\n**症状**: &#96;.await&#96; が足りないエラー\n\n**原因**: upstream の API 変更（TUIと同じ問題）\n\n**対策**: upstream/main をマージして解決\n\n### 2. ハンドラーの実装が未完成\n\n**症状**: プレースホルダーレスポンスを返す\n\n**原因**: 実際の supervisor/deep-research 実装との統合が未完成\n\n**対策**: \n&#96;&#96;&#96;rust\n// TODO in supervisor_tool_handler.rs\nasync fn execute_supervisor(params: &amp;SupervisorToolParam) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;String&gt; {\n    // 実際の codex_supervisor::Supervisor を呼び出す\n    use codex_supervisor::Supervisor;\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(config);\n    let result = supervisor.coordinate_goal(&amp;params.goal, params.agents.clone()).await?;\n    Ok(format!(\"{:?}\", result))\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🔮 次のステップ\n\n### 短期（1週間）\n\n1. **既存エラー修正**\n   - message_processor.rs の &#96;.await&#96; 追加\n   - upstream/main との統合\n\n2. **実装完成**\n   - supervisor_tool_handler の実装\n   - deep_research_tool_handler の実装\n\n3. **E2Eテスト**\n   - Cursor IDE での実動作確認\n   - スクリーンショット撮影\n\n### 中期（1ヶ月）\n\n4. **キャッシング**\n   - Deep Research 結果のキャッシュ\n   - API呼び出し削減\n\n5. **UI改善**\n   - 進捗表示\n   - エージェント状態表示\n\n6. **パフォーマンス最適化**\n   - 並列度の最適化\n   - レスポンスタイム短縮\n\n---\n\n## 📚 関連ドキュメント\n\n- **cursor-integration/README.md**: 詳細な使用方法\n- **AGENTS.md**: Multi-Agent戦略\n- **codex-rs/docs/security-profiles.md**: セキュリティ設定",

        "contents": "- &#96;main&#96; から作業ブランチ作成（例: &#96;merge-upstream-2025-12-20&#96;）\n- &#96;upstream/main&#96; を &#96;merge --no-ff&#96; で取り込み\n- 競合が出たら、ファイル単位で以下の優先順位で解消\n- **A: upstream の新仕様/セキュリティ修正が優先**\n- **B: 既存の独自機能は“必要な最小差分”で再適用**\n\n## 2) 独自機能 vs upstream 同等機能の仕分け（差分を削る）\n\n- &#96;upstream/main..origin/main&#96;（自分らだけのコミット）を一覧化し、テーマ別に分類\n- TUI入力/スラッシュコマンド（例: &#96;codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/chat_composer.rs&#96;）\n- Windows sandbox/exec（例: &#96;codex-rs/core/src/exec.rs&#96;, &#96;codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/lib.rs&#96;）\n- モデル/設定周り（例: &#96;codex-rs/core/src/*model*&#96;）\n- CI/GUI/テスト（例: &#96;.github/workflows/*&#96;, &#96;gui-tests/*&#96; など）\n- upstream 側に同等機能があるか、該当箇所を確認して以下のいずれかで決着\n- **置換**: upstream 実装へ寄せ、独自差分を削除\n- **維持**: upstream の流儀に合わせて独自機能を再適用\n\n## 3) ビルドを通す（codex-tui をゴールに合わせる）\n\n- Windows で詰まりやすいので、作業中は次を前提にする\n- &#96;CARGO_TARGET_DIR&#96; を短い固定パスへ\n- &#96;CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_INCREMENTAL=true&#96;\n- &#96;CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1&#96;（os error 5 の回避）\n- &#96;cargo build -p codex-tui --release --bin codex-tui&#96; を通し、エラーは上から順に修正\n\n## 4) フォーマット/静的チェック/テスト\n\n- Rust変更が入ったら &#96;just fmt&#96;（&#96;codex-rs&#96;）\n- 仕上げ前に &#96;just fix -p codex-tui&#96;（必要なら &#96;-p codex-core&#96; も）\n- テスト\n- &#96;cargo test -p codex-tui --lib bottom_pane::chat_composer&#96;\n- 余力があれば &#96;cargo test -p codex-tui&#96;\n- 共通/コアを触った場合は（確認を挟んで）&#96;cargo test --all-features&#96;\n\n## 5) 上書きインストール → 実機確認\n\n- &#96;cargo install --path tui --bin codex-tui --force&#96;\n- &#96;where codex-tui&#96; と &#96;codex-tui --version&#96; で差し替え確認\n- 手動確認\n- 入力が即時反映される",

        "contents": "# Codex v0.48.0 改良案リスト（実装ログから抽出）\n\n## 📋 抽出元\n- &#96;_docs/2025-10-16_05-07-09_音声通知設定_CodexとCursorの使い分け.md&#96;\n- &#96;_docs/2025-10-16_完全実装完了_最終報告.md&#96;\n- &#96;_docs/2025-10-15_ClaudeCode超え完成.md&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 改良案リスト\n\n### 1️⃣ 音声通知機能の改良\n\n#### 優先度: 中\n#### カテゴリ: UX改善\n\n**現状の課題:**\n- Cursor用スクリプト &#96;play-completion-sound.ps1&#96; が現在霊夢音声を使用\n- 魔理沙音声ファイルのパスが未確認（ファイルが見つからない）\n- Windows System通知音が手動設定のみ\n\n**改良案:**\n1. **Cursor用スクリプトの魔理沙化**\n   - &#96;play-completion-sound.ps1&#96; を魔理沙音声に変更\n   - ファイルパス確認後に実装\n   - 既存の霊夢音声はCodex CLI専用に維持\n\n2. **Windows System設定の自動化**\n   - &#96;set-windows-notification-sound.ps1&#96; の改良\n   - レジストリパス自動検出機能追加\n   - エラーハンドリング強化\n\n3. **追加キャラクター対応**\n   - 早苗、咲夜、妖夢などの音声追加\n   - キャラクター選択機能の実装\n   - &#96;config.toml&#96; でキャラクター切り替え可能に\n\n**実装ファイル:**\n- &#96;zapabob/scripts/play-completion-sound.ps1&#96;\n- &#96;zapabob/scripts/set-windows-notification-sound.ps1&#96;\n- &#96;config.toml&#96; (新規 &#96;[sounds]&#96; セクション)\n\n**期待効果:**\n- ユーザー体験の向上\n- キャラクターの使い分けによる視認性向上\n- 自動設定による導入障壁の低減\n\n---\n\n### 2️⃣ ThreeWayMerge の実装\n\n#### 優先度: 高\n#### カテゴリ: コア機能\n\n**現状の課題:**\n- &#96;MergeStrategy::ThreeWayMerge&#96; が未実装\n- コメント: \"// TODO: Implement 3-way merge logic\"\n- 現在は &#96;Sequential&#96; と &#96;LastWriteWins&#96; のみサポート\n\n**改良案:**\n1. **Git-style 3-way merge アルゴリズム実装**\n   - Base（共通祖先）、Ours（Agent A）、Theirs（Agent B）の3つを比較",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "# 2025-10-23 Phase 1: 公式リポジトリ統合完了\n\n## Summary\nOpenAI/codex upstream/mainとの統合に成功。独自機能（AgentRuntime, オーケストレーション, DeepResearch）を保持しながらマージ完了。\n\n## Phase 1.1: 上流変更の取り込み\n\n### マージ作業\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit fetch upstream\n# 最新コミット: 0b452714 (feat: use actual tokenizer for unified_exec truncation)\ngit merge upstream/main\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 競合解決\n2つのファイルで競合が発生:\n\n#### 1. &#96;codex-rs/core/Cargo.toml&#96;\n**競合内容:**\n- HEAD: &#96;dashmap = { workspace = true }&#96; (独自機能用)\n- upstream/main: &#96;codex-utils-tokenizer = { workspace = true }&#96; (公式機能)\n\n**解決方法:** 両方を保持\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\ncodex-utils-tokenizer = { workspace = true }\ndashmap = { workspace = true }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2. &#96;codex-rs/core/src/tools/mod.rs&#96;\n**競合内容:**\n- HEAD: 多数の独自インポート（orchestrator, agents関連）\n- upstream/main: 基本インポートのみ\n\n**解決方法:** すべての独自インポートを保持\n&#96;&#96;&#96;rust\nuse crate::function_tool::FunctionCallError;\nuse crate::tools::context::SharedTurnDiffTracker;\nuse crate::tools::events::{ToolEmitter, ToolEventCtx, ToolEventFailure, ToolEventStage};\nuse crate::tools::orchestrator::ToolOrchestrator;\nuse crate::tools::runtimes::apply_patch::{ApplyPatchRequest, ApplyPatchRuntime};\nuse crate::tools::runtimes::shell::{ShellRequest, ShellRuntime};\nuse crate::tools::sandboxing::{ToolCtx, ToolError};\nuse codex_utils_string::{take_bytes_at_char_boundary, take_last_bytes_at_char_boundary};\nuse codex_apply_patch::MaybeApplyPatchVerified;\nuse codex_apply_patch::maybe_parse_apply_patch_verified;\nuse codex_protocol::protocol::AskForApproval;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### マージコミット\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit add codex-rs/core/Cargo.toml codex-rs/core/src/tools/mod.rs\ngit commit -m \"merge: integrate upstream/main with custom features\"\n# コミットハッシュ: eb8274ee\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Phase 1.2: ビルドとテスト\n\n### ビルド実行\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd codex-rs\n$env:CARGO_TARGET_DIR = \"C:\\temp\\codex-target\"",

        "contents": "# Upstream Sync &amp; Merge 対応ログ\n\n**日時**: 2025-11-21 16:36:56  \n**ブランチ**: main  \n**計画**: Upstream Sync &amp; Merge Plan  \n\n## 作業概要\n- &#96;git fetch origin&#96; の後、&#96;git log main..origin/main&#96; と &#96;git diff --stat main origin/main&#96; で差分を把握し重点領域（&#96;codex-rs/Cargo.toml&#96;, &#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml&#96;, ならびに大量削除された &#96;.specstory/_docs&#96; 系履歴）を整理。\n- &#96;git merge --no-ff -X ours origin/main&#96; を実行して upstream と同期（結果は Already up to date）。\n- &#96;just fmt&#96; が Windows shell 未設定で失敗したため、代替として &#96;cargo fmt --all&#96; を直接実行し整形確認。\n- &#96;cargo test -p codex-cli&#96; を走らせて CLI crate のビルド健全性をチェック（0テスト構成だがビルド/リンク成功）。  \n\n## 詳細メモ\n\n### 1. Assess Divergence\n- ログ＆差分統計で upstream との差異が &#96;Cargo.toml&#96;（2 箇所）と &#96;.specstory&#96; / &#96;_docs&#96; 系大量削除に集中していることを確認。\n- GUI/TUI/CLI の観点で今回差分は Cargo メタデータのみだったため、追加コンフリクトは無しと判断。\n\n**実装状況**: [実装済み]  \n**動作確認**: [未確認]  \n**確認日時**: 2025-11-21  \n**備考**: &#96;git log origin/main..main&#96; でローカルが3コミット先行していることも確認済み。\n\n### 2. Merge origin/main into main\n- &#96;git merge --no-ff -X ours origin/main&#96; を実行。既に fast-forward 状態であったため新規コミットなし。\n- &#96;git status -sb&#96; でマージ後も既存の &#96;.specstory&#96; / &#96;_docs&#96; 変更のみが残っていることを再確認。\n\n**実装状況**: [実装済み]  \n**動作確認**: [未確認]  \n**確認日時**: 2025-11-21  \n**備考**: upstream との乖離ゼロのため reapply 作業不要。\n\n### 3. Stabilize Workspace\n- &#96;just fmt&#96; が shell 検出エラーで停止したため、&#96;cargo fmt --all&#96; を直接実行（nightly 限定オプション警告のみで終了）。\n- &#96;cargo test -p codex-cli&#96; を実施。テストケース自体は未定義だが crate のビルド＆リンクが成功し exit code 0 を確認。",

        "contents": "# 公式最新マージと独自機能優先コンフリクト解決\n\n**日時**: 2025-11-25 03:28:48  \n**バージョン**: v2.3.0  \n**ステータス**: ✅ 完了\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 概要\n\nTUI、GUI、CLIを正常起動していた差分や実装ログ、コミット履歴を参照して、現在の公式の最新（upstream/main）と現在の独自機能を優先してマージし、独自機能を優先してコンフリクトを解消したで！\n\n---\n\n## 📊 マージ前の状態\n\n### ローカル（独自機能）\n- **最新コミット**: &#96;b9f7397e1&#96; - QCエージェント統合と品質ベースマージ実装完了\n- **独自機能**:\n  - QCエージェント統合\n  - 開発モード選択機能\n  - TUI/GUI/CLI起動機能\n  - WebSocket RPCサーバー\n  - MCP統合\n\n### 公式（upstream/main）\n- **最新コミット**: &#96;486b1c4d9&#96; - consolidate world-writable-directories scanning\n- **主要更新**:\n  - execpolicy改善\n  - unified exec基本pruning戦略\n  - delegate cancellation修正\n  - セキュリティ改善\n  - Windows sandbox改善\n\n---\n\n## ✅ マージ実施内容\n\n### 1. 現在の変更をコミット\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit commit -m \"feat: QC agent integration and quality-based merge implementation\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**コミット内容**:\n- QCエージェント統合（&#96;qc_merger.rs&#96;, &#96;qc_logger.rs&#96;）\n- 開発モード選択機能（&#96;development_mode.rs&#96;）\n- 実装ログ（&#96;_docs/2025-11-25_*.md&#96;）\n\n### 2. upstream/mainをマージ\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit merge upstream/main --allow-unrelated-histories -X ours -m \"feat: Merge upstream/main with local custom features priority\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**マージ戦略**: &#96;-X ours&#96; - コンフリクト時にローカル版を優先\n\n### 3. コンフリクト解決\n\n**発生したコンフリクト**: 35ファイル\n\n#### 解決方針\n\n**独自機能を優先**:\n- &#96;protocol-ts/generate-ts&#96; - ローカル版を保持（独自機能）\n\n**公式機能を統合**:\n- &#96;app-server/&#96; - upstream版を採用（公式機能）\n- &#96;backend-client/&#96; - upstream版を採用（公式機能）\n- &#96;core/src/otel_init.rs&#96; - upstream版を採用（公式機能）",
```

```json
        "contents": "# Skills (experimental)\n\n&gt; **Warning:** This is an experimental and non-stable feature. If you depend on it, please expect breaking changes over the coming weeks and understand that there is currently no guarantee that this works well. Use at your own risk!\n\nCodex can automatically discover reusable \"skills\" you keep on disk. A skill is a small bundle with a name, a short description (what it does and when to use it), and an optional body of instructions you can open when needed. Codex injects only the name, description, and file path into the runtime context; the body stays on disk.\n\n## Enable skills\n\nSkills are behind the experimental &#96;skills&#96; feature flag and are disabled by default.\n\n- Enable in config (preferred): add the following to &#96;$CODEX_HOME/config.toml&#96; (usually &#96;~/.codex/config.toml&#96;) and restart Codex:\n\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n  [features]\n  skills = true\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Enable for a single run: launch Codex with &#96;codex --enable skills&#96;\n\n## Where skills live\n\n- Location (v1): &#96;~/.codex/skills/**/SKILL.md&#96; (recursive). Hidden entries and symlinks are skipped. Only files named exactly &#96;SKILL.md&#96; count.\n- Sorting: rendered by name, then path for stability.\n\n## File format\n\n- YAML frontmatter + body.\n  - Required:\n    - &#96;name&#96; (non-empty, ≤100 chars, sanitized to one line)\n    - &#96;description&#96; (non-empty, ≤500 chars, sanitized to one line)\n  - Extra keys are ignored. The body can contain any Markdown; it is not injected into context.\n\n## Loading and rendering\n\n- Loaded once at startup.\n- If valid skills exist, Codex appends a runtime-only &#96;## Skills&#96; section after &#96;AGENTS.md&#96;, one bullet per skill: &#96;- &lt;name&gt;: &lt;description&gt; (file: /absolute/path/to/SKILL.md)&#96;.\n- If no valid skills exist, the section is omitted. On-disk files are never modified.\n\n## Using skills\n\n- Mention a skill by name in a message using &#96;$&lt;skill-name&gt;&#96;.\n- In the TUI, you can also use &#96;/skills&#96; to browse and insert skills.\n\n## Validation and errors\n\n- Invalid skills (missing/invalid YAML, empty/over-length fields) trigger a blocking, dismissible startup modal in the TUI that lists each path and error. Errors are also logged. You can dismiss to continue (invalid skills are ignored) or exit. Fix SKILL.md files and restart to clear the modal.\n\n## Create a skill\n\n1. Create &#96;~/.codex/skills/&lt;skill-name&gt;/&#96;.",

        "contents": "use std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::RwLock;\n\nuse crate::skills::SkillLoadOutcome;\nuse crate::skills::loader::load_skills_from_roots;\nuse crate::skills::loader::skill_roots_for_cwd;\nuse crate::skills::system::install_system_skills;\npub struct SkillsManager {\n    codex_home: PathBuf,\n    cache_by_cwd: RwLock&lt;HashMap&lt;PathBuf, SkillLoadOutcome&gt;&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl SkillsManager {\n    pub fn new(codex_home: PathBuf) -&gt; Self {\n        if let Err(err) = install_system_skills(&amp;codex_home) {\n            tracing::error!(\"failed to install system skills: {err}\");\n        }\n\n        Self {\n            codex_home,\n            cache_by_cwd: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn skills_for_cwd(&amp;self, cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome {\n        self.skills_for_cwd_with_options(cwd, false)\n    }\n\n    pub fn skills_for_cwd_with_options(&amp;self, cwd: &amp;Path, force_reload: bool) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome {\n        let cached = match self.cache_by_cwd.read() {\n            Ok(cache) =&gt; cache.get(cwd).cloned(),\n            Err(err) =&gt; err.into_inner().get(cwd).cloned(),\n        };\n        if !force_reload &amp;&amp; let Some(outcome) = cached {\n            return outcome;\n        }\n\n        let roots = skill_roots_for_cwd(&amp;self.codex_home, cwd);\n        let outcome = load_skills_from_roots(roots);\n        match self.cache_by_cwd.write() {\n            Ok(mut cache) =&gt; {\n                cache.insert(cwd.to_path_buf(), outcome.clone());\n            }\n            Err(err) =&gt; {\n                err.into_inner().insert(cwd.to_path_buf(), outcome.clone());\n            }\n        }\n        outcome\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "use std::collections::HashSet;\n\nuse crate::skills::SkillLoadOutcome;\nuse crate::skills::SkillMetadata;\nuse crate::user_instructions::SkillInstructions;\nuse codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;\nuse codex_protocol::user_input::UserInput;\nuse tokio::fs;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub(crate) struct SkillInjections {\n    pub(crate) items: Vec&lt;ResponseItem&gt;,\n    pub(crate) warnings: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\npub(crate) async fn build_skill_injections(\n    inputs: &amp;[UserInput],\n    skills: Option&lt;&amp;SkillLoadOutcome&gt;,\n) -&gt; SkillInjections {\n    if inputs.is_empty() {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    }\n\n    let Some(outcome) = skills else {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    };\n\n    let mentioned_skills = collect_explicit_skill_mentions(inputs, &amp;outcome.skills);\n    if mentioned_skills.is_empty() {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = SkillInjections {\n        items: Vec::with_capacity(mentioned_skills.len()),\n        warnings: Vec::new(),\n    };\n\n    for skill in mentioned_skills {\n        match fs::read_to_string(&amp;skill.path).await {\n            Ok(contents) =&gt; {\n                result.items.push(ResponseItem::from(SkillInstructions {\n                    name: skill.name,\n                    path: skill.path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n                    contents,\n                }));\n            }\n            Err(err) =&gt; {\n                let message = format!(\n                    \"Failed to load skill {} at {}: {err:#}\",\n                    skill.name,\n                    skill.path.display()\n                );\n                result.warnings.push(message);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    result\n}\n\nfn collect_explicit_skill_mentions",

        "contents": "impl fmt::Display for SkillParseError {\n    fn fmt(&amp;self, f: &amp;mut fmt::Formatter&lt;'_&gt;) -&gt; fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            SkillParseError::Read(e) =&gt; write!(f, \"failed to read file: {e}\"),\n            SkillParseError::MissingFrontmatter =&gt; {\n                write!(f, \"missing YAML frontmatter delimited by ---\")\n            }\n            SkillParseError::InvalidYaml(e) =&gt; write!(f, \"invalid YAML: {e}\"),\n            SkillParseError::MissingField(field) =&gt; write!(f, \"missing field &#96;{field}&#96;\"),\n            SkillParseError::InvalidField { field, reason } =&gt; {\n                write!(f, \"invalid {field}: {reason}\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Error for SkillParseError {}\n\npub fn load_skills(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome {\n    load_skills_from_roots(skill_roots(config))\n}\n\npub(crate) struct SkillRoot {\n    pub(crate) path: PathBuf,\n    pub(crate) scope: SkillScope,\n}\n\npub(crate) fn load_skills_from_roots&lt;I&gt;(roots: I) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome\nwhere\n    I: IntoIterator&lt;Item = SkillRoot&gt;,\n{\n    let mut outcome = SkillLoadOutcome::default();\n    for root in roots {\n        discover_skills_under_root(&amp;root.path, root.scope, &amp;mut outcome);\n    }\n\n    let mut seen: HashSet&lt;String&gt; = HashSet::new();\n    outcome\n        .skills\n        .retain(|skill| seen.insert(skill.name.clone()));\n\n    outcome\n        .skills\n        .sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&amp;b.name).then_with(|| a.path.cmp(&amp;b.path)));\n\n    outcome\n}\n\npub(crate) fn user_skills_root(codex_home: &amp;Path) -&gt; SkillRoot {\n    SkillRoot {\n        path: codex_home.join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME),\n        scope: SkillScope::User,\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn system_skills_root(codex_home: &amp;Path) -&gt; SkillRoot {\n    SkillRoot {\n        path: system_cache_root_dir(codex_home),\n        scope: SkillScope::System,\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn admin_skills_root() -&gt; SkillRoot {\n    SkillRoot {\n        path: PathBuf::from(ADMIN_SKILLS_ROOT),\n        scope: SkillScope::Admin,\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn repo_skills_root(cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;SkillRoot&gt;",

        "contents": "use crate::skills::model::SkillMetadata;\n\npub fn render_skills_section(skills: &amp;[SkillMetadata]) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    if skills.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let mut lines: Vec&lt;String&gt; = Vec::new();\n    lines.push(\"## Skills\".to_string());\n    lines.push(\"These skills are discovered at startup from multiple local sources. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions.\".to_string());\n\n    for skill in skills {\n        let path_str = skill.path.to_string_lossy().replace('\\\\', \"/\");\n        let name = skill.name.as_str();\n        let description = skill.description.as_str();\n        lines.push(format!(\"- {name}: {description} (file: {path_str})\"));\n    }\n\n    lines.push(\n        r###\"- Discovery: Available skills are listed in project docs and may also appear in a runtime \"## Skills\" section (name + description + file path). These are the sources of truth; skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.\n- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with &#96;$SkillName&#96; or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.\n- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):\n  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its &#96;SKILL.md&#96;. Read only enough to follow the workflow.\n  2) If &#96;SKILL.md&#96; points to extra folders such as &#96;references/&#96;, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.\n  3) If &#96;scripts/&#96; exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.\n  4) If &#96;assets/&#96; or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.\n- Description as trigger: The YAML &#96;description&#96; in &#96;SKILL.md&#96; is the primary trigger signal; rely on it to decide applicability. If unsure, ask a brief clarification before proceeding.\n- Coordination and sequencing:\n  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.\n  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.\n- Context hygiene:\n  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.\n  - Avoid deeply nested references; prefer one-hop files explicitly linked from &#96;SKILL.md&#96;.\n  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.\n- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.\"###\n            .to_string(),\n    );\n\n    Some(lines.join(\"\\n\"))\n}",

        "contents": "pub enum Feature {\n    // Stable.\n    /// Create a ghost commit at each turn.\n    GhostCommit,\n    /// Include the view_image tool.\n    ViewImageTool,\n    /// Send warnings to the model to correct it on the tool usage.\n    ModelWarnings,\n    /// Enable the default shell tool.\n    ShellTool,\n\n    // Experimental\n    /// Use the single unified PTY-backed exec tool.\n    UnifiedExec,\n    /// Enable experimental RMCP features such as OAuth login.\n    RmcpClient,\n    /// Include the freeform apply_patch tool.\n    ApplyPatchFreeform,\n    /// Allow the model to request web searches.\n    WebSearchRequest,\n    /// Gate the execpolicy enforcement for shell/unified exec.\n    ExecPolicy,\n    /// Enable Windows sandbox (restricted token) on Windows.\n    WindowsSandbox,\n    /// Use the elevated Windows sandbox pipeline (setup + runner).\n    WindowsSandboxElevated,\n    /// Remote compaction enabled (only for ChatGPT auth)\n    RemoteCompaction,\n    /// Refresh remote models and emit AppReady once the list is available.\n    RemoteModels,\n    /// Allow model to call multiple tools in parallel (only for models supporting it).\n    ParallelToolCalls,\n    /// Experimental shell snapshotting.\n    ShellSnapshot,\n    /// Experimental TUI v2 (viewport) implementation.\n    Tui2,\n    /// Enable discovery and injection of skills.\n    Skills,\n}\n\nimpl Feature {\n    pub fn key(self) -&gt; &amp;'static str {\n        self.info().key\n    }\n\n    pub fn stage(self) -&gt; Stage {\n        self.info().stage\n    }\n\n    pub fn default_enabled(self) -&gt; bool {\n        self.info().default_enabled\n    }\n\n    fn info(self) -&gt; &amp;'static FeatureSpec {\n        FEATURES\n            .iter()\n            .find(|spec| spec.id == self)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| unreachable!(\"missing FeatureSpec for {:?}\", self))\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub struct LegacyFeatureUsage {\n    pub alias: String,\n    pub feature: Feature,\n}\n\n/// Holds the effective set of enabled features.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct Features {\n    enabled: BTreeSet&lt;Feature&gt;,",

        "contents": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSkill Initializer - Creates a new skill from template\n\nUsage:\n    init_skill.py &lt;skill-name&gt; --path &lt;path&gt; [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n\nExamples:\n    init_skill.py my-new-skill --path skills/public\n    init_skill.py my-new-skill --path skills/public --resources scripts,references\n    init_skill.py my-api-helper --path skills/private --resources scripts --examples\n    init_skill.py custom-skill --path /custom/location\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nMAX_SKILL_NAME_LENGTH = 64\nALLOWED_RESOURCES = {\"scripts\", \"references\", \"assets\"}\n\nSKILL_TEMPLATE = \"\"\"---\nname: {skill_name}\ndescription: [TODO: Complete and informative explanation of what the skill does and when to use it. Include WHEN to use this skill - specific scenarios, file types, or tasks that trigger it.]\n---\n\n# {skill_title}\n\n## Overview\n\n[TODO: 1-2 sentences explaining what this skill enables]\n\n## Structuring This Skill\n\n[TODO: Choose the structure that best fits this skill's purpose. Common patterns:\n\n**1. Workflow-Based** (best for sequential processes)\n- Works well when there are clear step-by-step procedures\n- Example: DOCX skill with \"Workflow Decision Tree\" -&gt; \"Reading\" -&gt; \"Creating\" -&gt; \"Editing\"\n- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Workflow Decision Tree -&gt; ## Step 1 -&gt; ## Step 2...\n\n**2. Task-Based** (best for tool collections)\n- Works well when the skill offers different operations/capabilities\n- Example: PDF skill with \"Quick Start\" -&gt; \"Merge PDFs\" -&gt; \"Split PDFs\" -&gt; \"Extract Text\"\n- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Quick Start -&gt; ## Task Category 1 -&gt; ## Task Category 2...\n\n**3. Reference/Guidelines** (best for standards or specifications)\n- Works well for brand guidelines, coding standards, or requirements\n- Example: Brand styling with \"Brand Guidelines\" -&gt; \"Colors\" -&gt; \"Typography\" -&gt; \"Features\"\n- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Guidelines -&gt; ## Specifications -&gt; ## Usage...\n\n**4. Capabilities-Based** (best for integrated systems)\n- Works well when the skill provides multiple interrelated features\n- Example: Product Management with \"Core Capabilities\" -&gt; numbered capability list\n- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Core Capabilities -&gt; ### 1. Feature -&gt; ### 2. Feature...\n\nPatterns can be mixed and matched as needed. Most skills combine patterns (e.g., start with task-based, add workflow for complex operations).\n\nDelete this entire \"Structuring This Skill\" section when done - it's just guidance.]\n\n## [TODO: Replace with the first main section based on chosen structure]\n\n[TODO: Add content here. See examples in existing skills:\n- Code samples for technical skills\n- Decision trees for complex workflows\n- Concrete examples with realistic user requests\n- References to scripts/templates/references as needed]\n\n## Resources (optional)\n\nCreate only the resource directories this skill actually needs. Delete this section if no resources are required.\n\n### scripts/\nExecutable code (Python/Bash/etc.) that can be run directly to perform specific operations.\n\n**Examples from other skills:**\n- PDF skill: &#96;fill_fillable_fields.py&#96;, &#96;extract_form_field_info.py&#96; - utilities for PDF manipulation\n- DOCX skill: &#96;document.py&#96;, &#96;utilities.py&#96; - Python modules for document processing\n\n**Appropriate for:** Python scripts, shell scripts, or any executable code that performs automation, data processing, or specific operations.\n\n**Note:** Scripts may be executed without loading into context, but can still be read by Codex for patching or environment adjustments.\n\n### references/\nDocumentation and reference material intended to be loaded into context to inform Codex's process and thinking.\n\n**Examples from other skills:**\n- Product management: &#96;communication.md&#96;, &#96;context_building.md&#96; - detailed workflow guides\n- BigQuery: API reference documentation and query examples\n- Finance: Schema documentation, company policies\n\n**Appropriate for:** In-depth documentation, API references, database schemas, comprehensive guides, or any detailed information that Codex should reference while working.\n\n### assets/\nFiles not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output Codex produces.\n\n**Examples from other skills:**\n- Brand styling: PowerPoint template files (.pptx), logo files\n- Frontend builder: HTML/React boilerplate project directories\n- Typography: Font files (.ttf, .woff2)\n\n**Appropriate for:** Templates, boilerplate code, document templates, images, icons, fonts, or any files meant to be copied or used in the final output.\n\n---\n\n**Not every skill requires all three types of resources.**\n\"\"\"\n\nEXAMPLE_SCRIPT = '''#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExample helper script for {skill_name}\n\nThis is a placeholder script that can be executed directly.\nReplace with actual implementation or delete if not needed.\n\nExample real scripts from other skills:\n- pdf/scripts/fill_fillable_fields.py - Fills PDF form fields\n- pdf/scripts/convert_pdf_to_images.py - Converts PDF pages to images\n\"\"\"\n\ndef main():\n    print(\"This is an example script for {skill_name}\")\n    # TODO: Add actual script logic here\n    # This could be data processing, file conversion, API calls, etc.\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "## Structuring This Skill",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "[TODO: Choose the structure that best fits this skill's purpose. Common patterns:",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "**1. Workflow-Based** (best for sequential processes)",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "- Works well when there are clear step-by-step procedures",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: DOCX skill with \"Workflow Decision Tree\" -&gt; \"Reading\" -&gt; \"Creating\" -&gt; \"Editing\"",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Workflow Decision Tree -&gt; ## Step 1 -&gt; ## Step 2...",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "**2. Task-Based** (best for tool collections)",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "- Works well when the skill offers different operations/capabilities",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: PDF skill with \"Quick Start\" -&gt; \"Merge PDFs\" -&gt; \"Split PDFs\" -&gt; \"Extract Text\"",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Quick Start -&gt; ## Task Category 1 -&gt; ## Task Category 2...",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "**3. Reference/Guidelines** (best for standards or specifications)",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "- Works well for brand guidelines, coding standards, or requirements",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: Brand styling with \"Brand Guidelines\" -&gt; \"Colors\" -&gt; \"Typography\" -&gt; \"Features\"",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Guidelines -&gt; ## Specifications -&gt; ## Usage...",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "**4. Capabilities-Based** (best for integrated systems)",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "- Works well when the skill provides multiple interrelated features",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: Product Management with \"Core Capabilities\" -&gt; numbered capability list",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "- Structure: ## Overview -&gt; ## Core Capabilities -&gt; ### 1. Feature -&gt; ### 2. Feature...",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "Patterns can be mixed and matched as needed. Most skills combine patterns (e.g., start with task-based, add workflow for complex operations).",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "Delete this entire \"Structuring This Skill\" section when done - it's just guidance.]",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "## [TODO: Replace with the first main section based on chosen structure]",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "[TODO: Add content here. See examples in existing skills:",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "- Code samples for technical skills",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "text": "- Decision trees for complex workflows",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "- Concrete examples with realistic user requests",

          },
          {
            "text": "- References to scripts/templates/references as needed]",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "## Resources (optional)",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "Create only the resource directories this skill actually needs. Delete this section if no resources are required.",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "### scripts/",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.) that can be run directly to perform specific operations.",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "**Examples from other skills:**",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "- PDF skill: &#96;fill_fillable_fields.py&#96;, &#96;extract_form_field_info.py&#96; - utilities for PDF manipulation",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "- DOCX skill: &#96;document.py&#96;, &#96;utilities.py&#96; - Python modules for document processing",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "**Appropriate for:** Python scripts, shell scripts, or any executable code that performs automation, data processing, or specific operations.",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "**Note:** Scripts may be executed without loading into context, but can still be read by Codex for patching or environment adjustments.",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "text": "### references/",
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "Documentation and reference material intended to be loaded into context to inform Codex's process and thinking.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "**Examples from other skills:**",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "- Product management: &#96;communication.md&#96;, &#96;context_building.md&#96; - detailed workflow guides",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "- BigQuery: API reference documentation and query examples",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "- Finance: Schema documentation, company policies",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": "**Appropriate for:** In-depth documentation, API references, database schemas, comprehensive guides, or any detailed information that Codex should reference while working.",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": "### assets/",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "Files not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output Codex produces.",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": "**Examples from other skills:**",
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "text": "- Brand styling: PowerPoint template files (.pptx), logo files",
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "- Frontend builder: HTML/React boilerplate project directories",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "text": "- Typography: Font files (.ttf, .woff2)",
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "text": "**Appropriate for:** Templates, boilerplate code, document templates, images, icons, fonts, or any files meant to be copied or used in the final output.",
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "**Not every skill requires all three types of resources.**",
```
