        "contents": "---\nname: skill-creator\ndescription: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\nmetadata:\n  short-description: Create or update a skill\n---\n\n# Skill Creator\n\nThis skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n\n## About Skills\n\nSkills are modular, self-contained packages that extend Codex's capabilities by providing\nspecialized knowledge, workflows, and tools. Think of them as \"onboarding guides\" for specific\ndomains or tasks—they transform Codex from a general-purpose agent into a specialized agent\nequipped with procedural knowledge that no model can fully possess.\n\n### What Skills Provide\n\n1. Specialized workflows - Multi-step procedures for specific domains\n2. Tool integrations - Instructions for working with specific file formats or APIs\n3. Domain expertise - Company-specific knowledge, schemas, business logic\n4. Bundled resources - Scripts, references, and assets for complex and repetitive tasks\n\n## Core Principles\n\n### Concise is Key\n\nThe context window is a public good. Skills share the context window with everything else Codex needs: system prompt, conversation history, other Skills' metadata, and the actual user request.\n\n**Default assumption: Codex is already very smart.** Only add context Codex doesn't already have. Challenge each piece of information: \"Does Codex really need this explanation?\" and \"Does this paragraph justify its token cost?\"\n\nPrefer concise examples over verbose explanations.\n\n### Set Appropriate Degrees of Freedom\n\nMatch the level of specificity to the task's fragility and variability:\n\n**High freedom (text-based instructions)**: Use when multiple approaches are valid, decisions depend on context, or heuristics guide the approach.\n\n**Medium freedom (pseudocode or scripts with parameters)**: Use when a preferred pattern exists, some variation is acceptable, or configuration affects behavior.\n\n**Low freedom (specific scripts, few parameters)**: Use when operations are fragile and error-prone, consistency is critical, or a specific sequence must be followed.",

        },
        "contents": "**Medium freedom (pseudocode or scripts with parameters)**: Use when a preferred pattern exists, some variation is acceptable, or configuration affects behavior.\n\n**Low freedom (specific scripts, few parameters)**: Use when operations are fragile and error-prone, consistency is critical, or a specific sequence must be followed.\n\nThink of Codex as exploring a path: a narrow bridge with cliffs needs specific guardrails (low freedom), while an open field allows many routes (high freedom).\n\n### Anatomy of a Skill\n\nEvery skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nskill-name/\n├── SKILL.md (required)\n│   ├── YAML frontmatter metadata (required)\n│   │   ├── name: (required)\n│   │   └── description: (required)\n│   └── Markdown instructions (required)\n└── Bundled Resources (optional)\n    ├── scripts/          - Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.)\n    ├── references/       - Documentation intended to be loaded into context as needed\n    └── assets/           - Files used in output (templates, icons, fonts, etc.)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### SKILL.md (required)\n\nEvery SKILL.md consists of:\n\n- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains &#96;name&#96; and &#96;description&#96; fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n\n#### Bundled Resources (optional)\n\n##### Scripts (&#96;scripts/&#96;)\n\nExecutable code (Python/Bash/etc.) for tasks that require deterministic reliability or are repeatedly rewritten.\n\n- **When to include**: When the same code is being rewritten repeatedly or deterministic reliability is needed\n- **Example**: &#96;scripts/rotate_pdf.py&#96; for PDF rotation tasks\n- **Benefits**: Token efficient, deterministic, may be executed without loading into context\n- **Note**: Scripts may still need to be read by Codex for patching or environment-specific adjustments",

        "contents": "use crate::config::Config;\nuse crate::git_info::resolve_root_git_project_for_trust;\nuse crate::skills::model::SkillError;\nuse crate::skills::model::SkillLoadOutcome;\nuse crate::skills::model::SkillMetadata;\nuse crate::skills::system::system_cache_root_dir;\nuse codex_protocol::protocol::SkillScope;\nuse dunce::canonicalize as normalize_path;\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse std::collections::HashSet;\nuse std::collections::VecDeque;\nuse std::error::Error;\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse tracing::error;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\nstruct SkillFrontmatter {\n    name: String,\n    description: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    metadata: SkillFrontmatterMetadata,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]\nstruct SkillFrontmatterMetadata {\n    #[serde(default, rename = \"short-description\")]\n    short_description: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\nconst SKILLS_FILENAME: &amp;str = \"SKILL.md\";\nconst SKILLS_DIR_NAME: &amp;str = \"skills\";\nconst REPO_ROOT_CONFIG_DIR_NAME: &amp;str = \".codex\";\nconst ADMIN_SKILLS_ROOT: &amp;str = \"/etc/codex/skills\";\nconst MAX_NAME_LEN: usize = 64;\nconst MAX_DESCRIPTION_LEN: usize = 1024;\nconst MAX_SHORT_DESCRIPTION_LEN: usize = MAX_DESCRIPTION_LEN;\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nenum SkillParseError {\n    Read(std::io::Error),\n    MissingFrontmatter,\n    InvalidYaml(serde_yaml::Error),\n    MissingField(&amp;'static str),\n    InvalidField { field: &amp;'static str, reason: String },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for SkillParseError {",

        "contents": "pub(crate) fn repo_skills_root(cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    let base = if cwd.is_dir() { cwd } else { cwd.parent()? };\n    let base = normalize_path(base).unwrap_or_else(|_| base.to_path_buf());\n\n    let repo_root =\n        resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(&amp;base).map(|root| normalize_path(&amp;root).unwrap_or(root));\n\n    let scope = SkillScope::Repo;\n    if let Some(repo_root) = repo_root.as_deref() {\n        for dir in base.ancestors() {\n            let skills_root = dir.join(REPO_ROOT_CONFIG_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME);\n            if skills_root.is_dir() {\n                return Some(SkillRoot {\n                    path: skills_root,\n                    scope,\n                });\n            }\n\n            if dir == repo_root {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let skills_root = base.join(REPO_ROOT_CONFIG_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME);\n    skills_root.is_dir().then_some(SkillRoot {\n        path: skills_root,\n        scope,\n    })\n}\n\npub(crate) fn skill_roots_for_cwd(codex_home: &amp;Path, cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Vec&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    let mut roots = Vec::new();\n\n    if let Some(repo_root) = repo_skills_root(cwd) {\n        roots.push(repo_root);\n    }\n\n    // Load order matters: we dedupe by name, keeping the first occurrence.\n    // Priority order: repo, user, system, then admin.\n    roots.push(user_skills_root(codex_home));\n    roots.push(system_skills_root(codex_home));\n    if cfg!(unix) {\n        roots.push(admin_skills_root());\n    }\n\n    roots\n}\n\nfn skill_roots(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; Vec&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    skill_roots_for_cwd(&amp;config.codex_home, &amp;config.cwd)\n}\n\nfn discover_skills_under_root(root: &amp;Path, scope: SkillScope,",

        "contents": "## Validation and errors\n\n- Invalid skills (missing/invalid YAML, empty/over-length fields) trigger a blocking, dismissible startup modal in the TUI that lists each path and error. Errors are also logged. You can dismiss to continue (invalid skills are ignored) or exit. Fix SKILL.md files and restart to clear the modal.\n\n## Create a skill\n\n1. Create &#96;~/.codex/skills/&lt;skill-name&gt;/&#96;.\n2. Add &#96;SKILL.md&#96;:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n   ---\n   name: your-skill-name\n   description: what it does and when to use it (&lt;=500 chars)\n   ---\n\n   # Optional body\n   Add instructions, references, examples, or scripts (kept on disk).\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Keep &#96;name&#96;/&#96;description&#96; within the limits; avoid newlines in those fields.\n4. Restart Codex to load the new skill.\n\n## Example\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmkdir -p ~/.codex/skills/pdf-processing\ncat &lt;&lt;'SKILL_EXAMPLE' &gt; ~/.codex/skills/pdf-processing/SKILL.md\n---\nname: pdf-processing\ndescription: Extract text and tables from PDFs; use when PDFs, forms, or document extraction are mentioned.\n---\n\n# PDF Processing\n- Use pdfplumber to extract text.\n- For form filling, see FORMS.md.\nSKILL_EXAMPLE\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "---\nname: skill-installer\ndescription: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos).\nmetadata:\n  short-description: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos\n---\n\n# Skill Installer\n\nHelps install skills. By default these are from https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated, but users can also provide other locations.\n\nUse the helper scripts based on the task:\n- List curated skills when the user asks what is available, or if the user uses this skill without specifying what to do.\n- Install from the curated list when the user provides a skill name.\n- Install from another repo when the user provides a GitHub repo/path (including private repos).\n\nInstall skills with the helper scripts.\n\n## Communication\n\nWhen listing curated skills, output approximately as follows, depending on the context of the user's request:\n\"\"\"\nSkills from {repo}:\n1. skill-1\n2. skill-2 (already installed)\n3. ...\nWhich ones would you like installed?\n\"\"\"\n\nAfter installing a skill, tell the user: \"Restart Codex to pick up new skills.\"\n\n## Scripts\n\nAll of these scripts use network, so when running in the sandbox, request escalation when running them.\n\n- &#96;scripts/list-curated-skills.py&#96; (prints curated list with installed annotations)\n- &#96;scripts/list-curated-skills.py --format json&#96;\n- &#96;scripts/install-skill-from-github.py --repo &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; --path &lt;path/to/skill&gt; [&lt;path/to/skill&gt; ...]&#96;\n- &#96;scripts/install-skill-from-github.py --url https://github.com/&lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;/tree/&lt;ref&gt;/&lt;path&gt;&#96;\n\n## Behavior and Options\n\n- Defaults to direct download for public GitHub repos.\n- If download fails with auth/permission errors, falls back to git sparse checkout.\n- Aborts if the destination skill directory already exists.\n- Installs into &#96;$CODEX_HOME/skills/&lt;skill-name&gt;&#96; (defaults to &#96;~/.codex/skills&#96;).\n- Multiple &#96;--path&#96; values install multiple skills in one run, each named from the path basename unless &#96;--name&#96; is supplied.\n- Options: &#96;--ref &lt;ref&gt;&#96; (default &#96;main&#96;), &#96;--dest &lt;path&gt;&#96;, &#96;--method auto|download|git&#96;.",

CodexResult&lt;CodexSpawnOk&gt; {\n        let (tx_sub, rx_sub) = async_channel::bounded(SUBMISSION_CHANNEL_CAPACITY);\n        let (tx_event, rx_event) = async_channel::unbounded();\n\n        let loaded_skills = config\n            .features\n            .enabled(Feature::Skills)\n            .then(|| skills_manager.skills_for_cwd(&amp;config.cwd));\n\n        if let Some(outcome) = &amp;loaded_skills {\n            for err in &amp;outcome.errors {\n                error!(\n                    \"failed to load skill {}: {}\",\n                    err.path.display(),\n                    err.message\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        let user_instructions = get_user_instructions(\n            &amp;config,\n            loaded_skills\n                .as_ref()\n                .map(|outcome| outcome.skills.as_slice()),\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        let exec_policy = load_exec_policy_for_features(&amp;config.features, &amp;config.codex_home)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|err| CodexErr::Fatal(format!(\"failed to load execpolicy: {err}\")))?;\n        let exec_policy = Arc::new(RwLock::new(exec_policy));\n\n        let config = Arc::new(config);\n        if config.features.enabled(Feature::RemoteModels)\n            &amp;&amp; let Err(err) = models_manager.refresh_available_models(&amp;config).await\n        {\n            error!(\"failed to refresh available models: {err:?}\");\n        }\n        let model = models_manager.get_model(&amp;config.model, &amp;config).await;\n        let session_configuration = SessionConfiguration {\n            provider: config.model_provider.clone(),\n            model: model.clone()",

        "contents": "    OAuth,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for McpAuthStatus {\n    fn fmt(&amp;self, f: &amp;mut fmt::Formatter&lt;'_&gt;) -&gt; fmt::Result {\n        let text = match self {\n            McpAuthStatus::Unsupported =&gt; \"Unsupported\",\n            McpAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn =&gt; \"Not logged in\",\n            McpAuthStatus::BearerToken =&gt; \"Bearer token\",\n            McpAuthStatus::OAuth =&gt; \"OAuth\",\n        };\n        f.write_str(text)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Response payload for &#96;Op::ListCustomPrompts&#96;.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct ListCustomPromptsResponseEvent {\n    pub custom_prompts: Vec&lt;CustomPrompt&gt;,\n}\n\n/// Response payload for &#96;Op::ListSkills&#96;.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct ListSkillsResponseEvent {\n    pub skills: Vec&lt;SkillsListEntry&gt;,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n#[ts(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum SkillScope {\n    User,\n    Repo,\n    System,\n    Admin,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct SkillMetadata {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: String,\n    #[ts(optional)]\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub short_description: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    pub path: PathBuf,\n    pub scope: SkillScope,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct SkillErrorInfo {\n    pub path: PathBuf,\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct SkillsListEntry {\n    pub cwd: PathBuf,\n    pub skills: Vec&lt;SkillMetadata&gt;,\n    pub errors: Vec&lt;SkillErrorInfo&gt;,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct SessionConfiguredEvent {\n    ///",

                  "lineNumber": 30,
                  "content": "The context window is a public good. Skills share the context window with everything else Codex needs: system prompt, conversation history, other Skills' metadata, and the actual user request."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 48,
                  "content": "### Anatomy of a Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 50,
                  "content": "Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 53,
                  "content": "skill-name/"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 54,
                  "content": "├── SKILL.md (required)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 65,
                  "content": "#### SKILL.md (required)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 67,
                  "content": "Every SKILL.md consists of:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 69,
                  "content": "- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains &#96;name&#96; and &#96;description&#96; fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 70,
                  "content": "- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 90,
                  "content": "- **Benefits**: Keeps SKILL.md lean, loaded only when Codex determines it's needed"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 91,
                  "content": "- **Best practice**: If files are large (&gt;10k words), include grep search patterns in SKILL.md"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 92,
                  "content": "- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 98,
                  "content": "- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 103,
                  "content": "#### What to Not Include in a Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 105,
                  "content": "A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 113,
                  "content": "The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 117,
                  "content": "Skills use a three-level loading system to manage context efficiently:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 120,
                  "content": "2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (&lt;5k words)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 125,
                  "content": "Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 127,
                  "content": "**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 150,
                  "content": "For Skills with multiple domains, organize content by domain to avoid loading irrelevant context:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 153,
                  "content": "bigquery-skill/"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 154,
                  "content": "├── SKILL.md (overview and navigation)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 164,
                  "content": "Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 168,
                  "content": "├── SKILL.md (workflow + provider selection)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 200,
                  "content": "- **Avoid deeply nested references** - Keep references one level deep from SKILL.md. All reference files should link directly from SKILL.md."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 203,
                  "content": "## Skill Creation Process"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 205,
                  "content": "Skill creation involves these steps:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 207,
                  "content": "1. Understand the skill with concrete examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 208,
                  "content": "2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 209,
                  "content": "3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 210,
                  "content": "4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 211,
                  "content": "5. Package the skill (run package_skill.py)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 216,
                  "content": "### Skill Naming"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 222,
                  "content": "- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 224,
                  "content": "### Step 1: Understanding the Skill with Concrete Examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 226,
                  "content": "Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 228,
                  "content": "To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 230,
                  "content": "For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 232,
                  "content": "- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 233,
                  "content": "- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 234,
                  "content": "- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 235,
                  "content": "- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 239,
                  "content": "Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 241,
                  "content": "### Step 2: Planning the Reusable Skill Contents"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 243,
                  "content": "To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 248,
                  "content": "Example: When building a &#96;pdf-editor&#96; skill to handle queries like \"Help me rotate this PDF,\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 251,
                  "content": "2. A &#96;scripts/rotate_pdf.py&#96; script would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 253,
                  "content": "Example: When designing a &#96;frontend-webapp-builder&#96; skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 256,
                  "content": "2. An &#96;assets/hello-world/&#96; template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 258,
                  "content": "Example: When building a &#96;big-query&#96; skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 261,
                  "content": "2. A &#96;references/schema.md&#96; file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 263,
                  "content": "To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 265,
                  "content": "### Step 3: Initializing the Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 267,
                  "content": "At this point, it is time to actually create the skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 269,
                  "content": "Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists, and iteration or packaging is needed. In this case, continue to the next step."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 271,
                  "content": "When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the &#96;init_skill.py&#96; script.                 },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 276,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py &lt;skill-name&gt; --path &lt;output-directory&gt; [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 282,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 283,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public --resources scripts,references"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 284,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public --resources scripts --examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 289,
                  "content": "- Creates the skill directory at the specified path"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 290,
                  "content": "- Generates a SKILL.md template with proper frontmatter and TODO placeholders"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 294,
                  "content": "After initialization, customize the SKILL.md and add resources as needed. If you used &#96;--examples&#96;, replace or delete placeholder files."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 296,
                  "content": "### Step 4: Edit the Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 298,
                  "content": "When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 302,
                  "content": "Consult these helpful guides based on your skill's needs:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 307,
                  "content": "These files contain established best practices for effective skill design."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 309,
                  "content": "#### Start with Reusable Skill Contents"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 311,
                  "content": "To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: &#96;scripts/&#96;, &#96;references/&#96;, and &#96;assets/&#96; files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a &#96;brand-guidelines&#96; skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in &#96;assets/&#96;, or documentation to store in &#96;references/&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 315,
                  "content": "If you used &#96;--examples&#96;, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 317,
                  "content": "#### Update SKILL.md"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 325,

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 326,
                  "content": "- &#96;description&#96;: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 327,
                  "content": "  - Include both what the Skill does and specific triggers/contexts for when to use it."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 328,
                  "content": "  - Include all \"when to use\" information here - Not in the body. The body is only loaded after triggering, so \"When to Use This Skill\" sections in the body are not helpful to Codex."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 329,
                  "content": "  - Example description for a &#96;docx&#96; skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Use when Codex needs to work with professional documents (.docx files) for: (1) Creating new documents, (2) Modifying or editing content, (3) Working with tracked changes, (4) Adding comments, or any other document tasks\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 335,
                  "content": "Write instructions for using the skill and its bundled resources."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 337,
                  "content": "### Step 5: Packaging a Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 339,
                  "content": "Once development of the skill is complete, it must be packaged into a distributable .skill file that gets shared with the user. The packaging process automatically validates the skill first to ensure it meets all requirements:"

                },

                  "lineNumber": 348,

                },

                {

                },

        "contents": "    /// Request to shut down codex instance.\n    Shutdown,\n\n    /// Execute a user-initiated one-off shell command (triggered by \"!cmd\").\n    ///\n    /// The command string is executed using the user's default shell and may\n    /// include shell syntax (pipes, redirects, etc.). Output is streamed via\n    /// &#96;ExecCommand*&#96; events and the UI regains control upon &#96;TaskComplete&#96;.\n    RunUserShellCommand {\n        /// The raw command string after '!'\n        command: String,\n    },\n\n    /// Request the list of available models.\n    ListModels,\n}\n\n/// Determines the conditions under which the user is consulted to approve\n/// running the command proposed by Codex.\n#[derive(\n    Debug,\n    Clone,\n    Copy,\n    Default,\n    PartialEq,\n    Eq,\n    Hash,\n    Serialize,\n    Deserialize,\n    Display,\n    JsonSchema,\n    TS,\n)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"kebab-case\")]\n#[strum(serialize_all = \"kebab-case\")]\npub enum AskForApproval {\n    /// Under this policy, only \"known safe\" commands—as determined by\n    /// &#96;is_safe_command()&#96;—that **only read files** are auto‑approved.\n    /// Everything else will ask the user to approve.\n    #[serde(rename = \"untrusted\")]\n    #[strum(serialize = \"untrusted\")]\n    UnlessTrusted,\n\n    /// *All* commands are auto‑approved, but they are expected to run inside a\n    /// sandbox where network access is disabled and writes are confined to a\n    /// specific set of paths. If the command fails, it will be escalated to\n    /// the user to approve execution without a sandbox.\n    OnFailure,\n\n    /// The model decides when to ask the user for approval.\n    #[default]\n    OnRequest,\n\n    /// Never ask the user to approve commands. Failures are immediately returned\n    /// to the model, and never escalated to the user for approval.\n    Never,\n}\n\n/// Represents whether outbound network access is available to the agent.\n#[derive(\n    Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Display, Default, JsonSchema, TS,\n)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"kebab-case\")]\n#[strum(serialize_all = \"kebab-case\")]\npub enum NetworkAccess",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\codex-rs\\app-server\\README.md",

          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 85
          }
        },
        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## API Overview\n\n- &#96;thread/start&#96; — create a new thread; emits &#96;thread/started&#96; and auto-subscribes you to turn/item events for that thread.\n- &#96;thread/resume&#96; — reopen an existing thread by id so subsequent &#96;turn/start&#96; calls append to it.\n- &#96;thread/list&#96; — page through stored rollouts; supports cursor-based pagination and optional &#96;modelProviders&#96; filtering.\n- &#96;thread/archive&#96; — move a thread’s rollout file into the archived directory; returns &#96;{}&#96; on success.\n- &#96;turn/start&#96; — add user input to a thread and begin Codex generation; responds with the initial &#96;turn&#96; object and streams &#96;turn/started&#96;, &#96;item/*&#96;, and &#96;turn/completed&#96; notifications.\n- &#96;turn/interrupt&#96; — request cancellation of an in-flight turn by &#96;(thread_id, turn_id)&#96;; success is an empty &#96;{}&#96; response and the turn finishes with &#96;status: \"interrupted\"&#96;.\n- &#96;review/start&#96; — kick off Codex’s automated reviewer for a thread; responds like &#96;turn/start&#96; and emits &#96;item/started&#96;/&#96;item/completed&#96; notifications with &#96;enteredReviewMode&#96; and &#96;exitedReviewMode&#96; items, plus a final assistant &#96;agentMessage&#96; containing the review.\n- &#96;command/exec&#96; — run a single command under the server sandbox without starting a thread/turn (handy for utilities and validation).\n- &#96;model/list&#96; — list available models (with reasoning effort options).\n- &#96;skills/list&#96; — list skills for one or more &#96;cwd&#96; values (optional &#96;forceReload&#96;).\n- &#96;mcpServer/oauth/login&#96; — start an OAuth login for a configured MCP server; returns an &#96;authorization_url&#96; and later emits &#96;mcpServer/oauthLogin/completed&#96; once the browser flow finishes.\n- &#96;mcpServerStatus/list&#96; — enumerate configured MCP servers with their tools, resources, resource templates, and auth status; supports cursor+limit pagination.\n- &#96;feedback/upload&#96; — submit a feedback report (classification + optional reason/logs and conversation_id); returns the tracking thread id.\n- &#96;command/exec&#96; — run a single command under the server sandbox without starting a thread/turn (handy for utilities and validation).\n- &#96;config/read&#96; — fetch the effective config on disk after resolving config layering.",

        "contents": "/*\nModule: runtimes\n\nConcrete ToolRuntime implementations for specific tools. Each runtime stays\nsmall and focused and reuses the orchestrator for approvals + sandbox + retry.\n*/\nuse crate::exec::ExecExpiration;\nuse crate::sandboxing::CommandSpec;\nuse crate::sandboxing::SandboxPermissions;\nuse crate::shell::Shell;\nuse crate::tools::sandboxing::ToolError;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\npub mod apply_patch;\npub mod shell;\npub mod unified_exec;\n\n/// Shared helper to construct a CommandSpec from a tokenized command line.\n/// Validates that at least a program is present.\npub(crate) fn build_command_spec(\n    command: &amp;[String],\n    cwd: &amp;Path,\n    env: &amp;HashMap&lt;String, String&gt;,\n    expiration: ExecExpiration,\n    sandbox_permissions: SandboxPermissions,\n    justification: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;CommandSpec, ToolError&gt; {\n    let (program, args) = command\n        .split_first()\n        .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::Rejected(\"command args are empty\".to_string()))?;\n    Ok(CommandSpec {\n        program: program.clone(),\n        args: args.to_vec(),\n        cwd: cwd.to_path_buf(),\n        env: env.clone(),\n        expiration,\n        sandbox_permissions,\n        justification,\n    })\n}\n\n/// POSIX-only helper: for commands produced by &#96;Shell::derive_exec_args&#96;\n/// for Bash/Zsh/sh of the form &#96;[shell_path, \"-lc\", \"&lt;script&gt;\"]&#96;, and\n/// when a snapshot is configured on the session shell, rewrite the argv\n/// to a single non-login shell that sources the snapshot before running\n/// the original script:\n///\n///   shell -lc \"&lt;script&gt;\"\n///   =&gt; shell -c \". SNAPSHOT &amp;&amp; &lt;script&gt;\"\n///\n/// On non-POSIX shells or non-matching commands this is a no-op.\npub(crate) fn maybe_wrap_shell_lc_with_snapshot(\n    command: &amp;[String],\n    session_shell: &amp;Shell,\n) -&gt; Vec&lt;String&gt;",

        "contents": "    fn dispatch_command(&amp;mut self, cmd: SlashCommand) {\n        if !cmd.available_during_task() &amp;&amp; self.bottom_pane.is_task_running() {\n            let message = format!(\n                \"'/{}' is disabled while a task is in progress.\",\n                cmd.command()\n            );\n            self.add_to_history(history_cell::new_error_event(message));\n            self.request_redraw();\n            return;\n        }\n        match cmd {\n            SlashCommand::Feedback =&gt; {\n                // Step 1: pick a category (UI built in feedback_view)\n                let params =\n                    crate::bottom_pane::feedback_selection_params(self.app_event_tx.clone());\n                self.bottom_pane.show_selection_view(params);\n                self.request_redraw();\n            }\n            SlashCommand::New =&gt; {\n                self.app_event_tx.send(AppEvent::NewSession);\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Resume =&gt; {\n                self.app_event_tx.send(AppEvent::OpenResumePicker);\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Init =&gt; {\n                let init_target = self.config.cwd.join(DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME);\n                if init_target.exists() {\n                    let message = format!(\n                        \"{DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME} already exists here. Skipping /init to avoid overwriting it.\"\n                    );\n                    self.add_info_message(message, None);\n                    return;\n                }\n                const INIT_PROMPT: &amp;str = include_str!(\"../prompt_for_init_command.md\");\n                self.submit_user_message(INIT_PROMPT.to_string().into());\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Compact =&gt; {\n                self.clear_token_usage();\n                self.app_event_tx.send(AppEvent::CodexOp(Op::Compact));\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Review =&gt; {\n                self.open_review_popup();\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Model =&gt; {\n                self.open_model_popup();\n            }\n            SlashCommand::Approvals =&gt; {\n                self.open_approvals_popup();",

{\n            let args_no_connector = trim_at_connector(tail);\n            let has_files_flag = args_no_connector.iter().any(|a| a == \"--files\");\n            let non_flags: Vec&lt;&amp;String&gt;           "endPosition": {

        },
        "contents": "- &#96;command/exec&#96; — run a single command under the server sandbox without starting a thread/turn (handy for utilities and validation).\n- &#96;config/read&#96; — fetch the effective config on disk after resolving config layering.\n- &#96;config/value/write&#96; — write a single config key/value to the user's config.toml on disk.\n- &#96;config/batchWrite&#96; — apply multiple config edits atomically to the user's config.toml on disk.\n\n### Example: Start or resume a thread\n\nStart a fresh thread when you need a new Codex conversation.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{ \"method\": \"thread/start\", \"id\": 10, \"params\": {\n    // Optionally set config settings. If not specified, will use the user's\n    // current config settings.\n    \"model\": \"gpt-5.1-codex\",\n    \"cwd\": \"/Users/me/project\",\n    \"approvalPolicy\": \"never\",\n    \"sandbox\": \"workspaceWrite\",\n} }\n{ \"id\": 10, \"result\": {\n    \"thread\": {\n        \"id\": \"thr_123\",\n        \"preview\": \"\",\n        \"modelProvider\": \"openai\",\n        \"createdAt\": 1730910000\n    }\n} }\n{ \"method\": \"thread/started\", \"params\": { \"thread\": { … } } }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo continue a stored session, call &#96;thread/resume&#96; with the &#96;thread.id&#96; you previously recorded. The response shape matches &#96;thread/start&#96;, and no additional notifications are emitted:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{ \"method\": \"thread/resume\", \"id\": 11, \"params\": { \"threadId\": \"thr_123\" } }\n{ \"id\": 11, \"result\": { \"thread\": { \"id\": \"thr_123\", … } } }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: List threads (with pagination &amp; filters)\n\n&#96;thread/list&#96; lets you render a history UI. Pass any combination of:\n\n- &#96;cursor&#96; — opaque string from a prior response; omit for the first page.\n- &#96;limit&#96; — server defaults to a reasonable page size if unset.\n- &#96;modelProviders&#96; — restrict results to specific providers; unset, null, or an empty array will include all providers.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{ \"method\": \"thread/list\", \"id\": 20, \"params\": {\n    \"cursor\": null,\n    \"limit\": 25,\n} }\n{ \"id\": 20, \"result\": {\n    \"data\": [\n        { \"id\": \"thr_a\", \"preview\": \"Create a TUI\", \"modelProvider\": \"openai\", \"createdAt\": 1730831111 },",

        "contents": "# codex-app-server\n\n&#96;codex app-server&#96; is the interface Codex uses to power rich interfaces such as the [Codex VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=openai.chatgpt).\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Protocol](#protocol)\n- [Message Schema](#message-schema)\n- [Core Primitives](#core-primitives)\n- [Lifecycle Overview](#lifecycle-overview)\n- [Initialization](#initialization)\n- [API Overview](#api-overview)\n- [Events](#events)\n- [Auth endpoints](#auth-endpoints)\n\n## Protocol\n\nSimilar to [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/), &#96;codex app-server&#96; supports bidirectional communication, streaming JSONL over stdio. The protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0, though the &#96;\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\"&#96; header is omitted.\n\n## Message Schema\n\nCurrently, you can dump a TypeScript version of the schema using &#96;codex app-server generate-ts&#96;, or a JSON Schema bundle via &#96;codex app-server generate-json-schema&#96;. Each output is specific to the version of Codex you used to run the command, so the generated artifacts are guaranteed to match that version.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ncodex app-server generate-ts --out DIR\ncodex app-server generate-json-schema --out DIR\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Core Primitives\n\nThe API exposes three top level primitives representing an interaction between a user and Codex:\n\n- **Thread**: A conversation between a user and the Codex agent. Each thread contains multiple turns.\n- **Turn**: One turn of the conversation, typically starting with a user message and finishing with an agent message. Each turn contains multiple items.\n- **Item**: Represents user inputs and agent outputs as part of the turn, persisted and used as the context for future conversations. Example items include user message, agent reasoning, agent message, shell command, file edit, etc.\n\nUse the thread APIs to create, list, or archive conversations. Drive a conversation with turn APIs and stream progress via turn notifications.\n\n## Lifecycle Overview\n\n- Initialize once: Immediately after launching the codex app-server process, send an &#96;initialize&#96; request with your client metadata, then emit an &#96;initialized&#96; notification. Any other request before this handshake gets rejected.\n- Start (or resume) a thread: Call &#96;thread/start&#96; to open a fresh conversation. The response returns the thread object and you’ll also get a &#96;thread/started&#96; notification. If you’re continuing an existing conversation, call &#96;thread/resume&#96; with its ID instead.",

        "contents": "## Lifecycle Overview\n\n- Initialize once: Immediately after launching the codex app-server process, send an &#96;initialize&#96; request with your client metadata, then emit an &#96;initialized&#96; notification. Any other request before this handshake gets rejected.\n- Start (or resume) a thread: Call &#96;thread/start&#96; to open a fresh conversation. The response returns the thread object and you’ll also get a &#96;thread/started&#96; notification. If you’re continuing an existing conversation, call &#96;thread/resume&#96; with its ID instead.\n- Begin a turn: To send user input, call &#96;turn/start&#96; with the target &#96;threadId&#96; and the user's input. Optional fields let you override model, cwd, sandbox policy, etc. This immediately returns the new turn object and triggers a &#96;turn/started&#96; notification.\n- Stream events: After &#96;turn/start&#96;, keep reading JSON-RPC notifications on stdout. You’ll see &#96;item/started&#96;, &#96;item/completed&#96;, deltas like &#96;item/agentMessage/delta&#96;, tool progress, etc. These represent streaming model output plus any side effects (commands, tool calls, reasoning notes).\n- Finish the turn: When the model is done (or the turn is interrupted via making the &#96;turn/interrupt&#96; call), the server sends &#96;turn/completed&#96; with the final turn state and token usage.\n\n## Initialization\n\nClients must send a single &#96;initialize&#96; request before invoking any other method, then acknowledge with an &#96;initialized&#96; notification. The server returns the user agent string it will present to upstream services; subsequent requests issued before initialization receive a &#96;\"Not initialized\"&#96; error, and repeated &#96;initialize&#96; calls receive an &#96;\"Already initialized\"&#96; error.\n\nApplications building on top of &#96;codex app-server&#96; should identify themselves via the &#96;clientInfo&#96; parameter.\n\nExample (from OpenAI's official VSCode extension):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"method\": \"initialize\",\n  \"id\": 0,\n  \"params\": {\n    \"clientInfo\": {\n      \"name\": \"codex-vscode\",\n      \"title\": \"Codex VS Code Extension\",\n      \"version\": \"0.1.0\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## API Overview\n\n- &#96;thread/start&#96; — create a new thread; emits &#96;thread/started&#96; and auto-subscribes you to turn/item events for that thread.",

        "contents": "use crate::command_safety::windows_safe_commands::is_safe_command_windows;\n\npub fn is_known_safe_command(command: &amp;[String]) -&gt; bool {\n    let command: Vec&lt;String&gt; = command\n        .iter()\n        .map(|s| {\n            if s == \"zsh\" {\n                \"bash\".to_string()\n            } else {\n                s.clone()\n            }\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    if is_safe_command_windows(&amp;command) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    if is_safe_to_call_with_exec(&amp;command) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Support &#96;bash -lc \"...\"&#96; where the script consists solely of one or\n    // more \"plain\" commands (only bare words / quoted strings) combined with\n    // a conservative allow‑list of shell operators that themselves do not\n    // introduce side effects ( \"&amp;&amp;\", \"||\", \";\", and \"|\" ). If every\n    // individual command in the script is itself a known‑safe command, then\n    // the composite expression is considered safe.\n    if let Some(all_commands) = parse_shell_lc_plain_commands(&amp;command)\n        &amp;&amp; !all_commands.is_empty()\n        &amp;&amp; all_commands\n            .iter()\n            .all(|cmd| is_safe_to_call_with_exec(cmd))\n    {\n        return true;\n    }\n    false\n}\n\nfn is_safe_to_call_with_exec(command: &amp;[String]) -&gt; bool",

        "contents": "pub enum CodexErr {\n    #[error(\"turn aborted. Something went wrong? Hit &#96;/feedback&#96; to report the issue.\")]\n    TurnAborted,\n\n    /// Returned by ResponsesClient when the SSE stream disconnects or errors out **after** the HTTP\n    /// handshake has succeeded but **before** it finished emitting &#96;response.completed&#96;.\n    ///\n    /// The Session loop treats this as a transient error and will automatically retry the turn.\n    ///\n    /// Optionally includes the requested delay before retrying the turn.\n    #[error(\"stream disconnected before completion: {0}\")]\n    Stream(String, Option&lt;Duration&gt;),\n\n    #[error(\n        \"Codex ran out of room in the model's context window. Start a new conversation or clear earlier history before retrying.\"\n    )]\n    ContextWindowExceeded,\n\n    #[error(\"no conversation with id: {0}\")]\n    ConversationNotFound(ConversationId),\n\n    #[error(\"session configured event was not the first event in the stream\")]\n    SessionConfiguredNotFirstEvent,\n\n    /// Returned by run_command_stream when the spawned child process timed out (10s).\n    #[error(\"timeout waiting for child process to exit\")]\n    Timeout,\n\n    /// Returned by run_command_stream when the child could not be spawned (its stdout/stderr pipes\n    /// could not be captured). Analogous to the previous &#96;CodexError::Spawn&#96; variant.\n    #[error(\"spawn failed: child stdout/stderr not captured\")]\n    Spawn,\n\n    /// Returned by run_command_stream when the user pressed Ctrl‑C (SIGINT).         "contents": "pub enum ReviewDecision {\n    /// User has approved this command and the agent should execute it.\n    Approved,\n\n    /// User has approved this command and wants to apply the proposed execpolicy\n    /// amendment so future matching commands are permitted.\n    ApprovedExecpolicyAmendment {\n        proposed_execpolicy_amendment: ExecPolicyAmendment,\n    },\n\n    /// User has approved this command and wants to automatically approve any\n    /// future identical instances (&#96;command&#96; and &#96;cwd&#96; match exactly) for the\n    /// remainder of the session.\n    ApprovedForSession,\n\n    /// User has denied this command and the agent should not execute it, but\n    /// it should continue the session and try something else.\n    #[default]\n    Denied,\n\n    /// User has denied this command and the agent should not do anything until\n    /// the user's next command.\n    Abort,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, JsonSchema, TS)]\n#[serde(tag = \"type\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n#[ts(tag = \"type\")]\npub enum FileChange {\n    Add {\n        content: String,\n    },\n    Delete {\n        content: String,\n    },\n    Update {\n        unified_diff: String,\n        move_path: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,\n    },\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct Chunk {\n    /// 1-based line index of the first line in the original file\n    pub orig_index: u32,\n    pub deleted_lines: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n    pub inserted_lines: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]\npub struct TurnAbortedEvent {\n    pub reason: TurnAbortReason,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, JsonSchema, TS)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum TurnAbortReason {\n    Interrupted,\n    Replaced,\n    ReviewEnded,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::items::UserMessageItem;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "impl ClientHandler for LoggingClientHandler {\n    async fn create_elicitation(\n        &amp;self,\n        request: CreateElicitationRequestParam,\n        context: RequestContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;CreateElicitationResult, rmcp::ErrorData&gt; {\n        let id = match context.id {\n            RequestId::String(id) =&gt; mcp_types::RequestId::String(id.to_string()),\n            RequestId::Number(id) =&gt; mcp_types::RequestId::Integer(id),\n        };\n        (self.send_elicitation)(id, request)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|err| rmcp::ErrorData::internal_error(err.to_string(), None))\n    }\n\n    async fn on_cancelled(\n        &amp;self,\n        params: CancelledNotificationParam,\n        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,\n    ) {\n        info!(\n            \"MCP server cancelled request (request_id: {}, reason: {:?})\",\n            params.request_id, params.reason\n        );\n    }\n\n    async fn on_progress(\n        &amp;self,\n        params: ProgressNotificationParam,\n        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,\n    ) {\n        info!(\n            \"MCP server progress notification (token: {:?}, progress: {}, total: {:?}, message: {:?})\",\n            params.progress_token, params.progress, params.total, params.message\n        );\n    }\n\n    async fn on_resource_updated(\n        &amp;self,\n        params: ResourceUpdatedNotificationParam,\n        _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;,\n    ) {\n        info!(\"MCP server resource updated (uri: {})\", params.uri);\n    }\n\n    async fn on_resource_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {\n        info!(\"MCP server resource list changed\");\n    }\n\n    async fn on_tool_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {\n        info!(\"MCP server tool list changed\");\n    }\n\n    async fn on_prompt_list_changed(&amp;self, _context: NotificationContext&lt;RoleClient&gt;) {\n        info!(\"MCP server prompt list changed\");\n    }\n\n    fn get_info(&amp;self) -&gt; ClientInfo {\n        self.client_info.clone()\n    }",

        "contents": "    pub fn record_responses(&amp;self, handle_responses_span: &amp;Span, event: &amp;ResponseEvent) {\n        handle_responses_span.record(\"otel.name\", OtelManager::responses_type(event));\n\n        match event {\n            ResponseEvent::OutputItemDone(item) =&gt; {\n                handle_responses_span.record(\"from\", \"output_item_done\");\n                if let ResponseItem::FunctionCall { name, .. } = &amp;item {\n                    handle_responses_span.record(\"tool_name\", name.as_str());\n                }\n            }\n            ResponseEvent::OutputItemAdded(item) =&gt; {\n                handle_responses_span.record(\"from\", \"output_item_added\");\n                if let ResponseItem::FunctionCall { name, .. } = &amp;item {\n                    handle_responses_span.record(\"tool_name\", name.as_str());\n                }\n            }\n            _ =&gt; {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub fn conversation_starts(\n        &amp;self,\n        provider_name: &amp;str,",

        "contents": "    pub fn conversation_starts(\n        &amp;self,\n        provider_name: &amp;str,\n        reasoning_effort: Option&lt;ReasoningEffort&gt;,\n        reasoning_summary: ReasoningSummary,\n        context_window: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n        max_output_tokens: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n        auto_compact_token_limit: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n        approval_policy: AskForApproval,\n        sandbox_policy: SandboxPolicy,\n        mcp_servers: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt;,\n        active_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) {\n        tracing::event!(\n            tracing::Level::INFO,\n            event.name = \"codex.conversation_starts\",\n            event.timestamp = %timestamp(),\n            conversation.id = %self.metadata.conversation_id,\n            app.version = %self.metadata.app_version,\n            auth_mode = self.metadata.auth_mode,\n            user.account_id = self.metadata.account_id,\n            user.email = self.metadata.account_email,\n            terminal.type = %self.metadata.terminal_type,\n            model = %self.metadata.model,\n            slug = %self.metadata.slug,\n            provider_name = %provider_name,\n            reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort.map(|e| e.to_string()),\n            reasoning_summary = %reasoning_summary,\n            context_window = context_window,\n            max_output_tokens = max_output_tokens,\n            auto_compact_token_limit = auto_compact_token_limit,\n            approval_policy = %approval_policy,\n            sandbox_policy = %sandbox_policy,\n            mcp_servers = mcp_servers.join(\", \"),\n            active_profile = active_profile,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub async fn log_request&lt;F, Fut&gt;",

          }
        },
        "contents": "    pub fn from(settings: &amp;OtelSettings) -&gt; Result&lt;Option&lt;Self&gt;, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {\n        let log_enabled = !matches!(settings.exporter, OtelExporter::None);\n        let trace_enabled = !matches!(settings.trace_exporter, OtelExporter::None);\n\n        if !log_enabled &amp;&amp; !trace_enabled {\n            debug!(\"No exporter enabled in OTLP settings.\");\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n\n        let resource = make_resource(settings);\n        let logger = log_enabled\n            .then(|| build_logger(&amp;resource, &amp;settings.exporter))\n            .transpose()?;\n\n        let tracer_provider = trace_enabled\n            .then(|| build_tracer_provider(&amp;resource, &amp;settings.trace_exporter))\n            .transpose()?;\n\n        let tracer = tracer_provider\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|provider| provider.tracer(settings.service_name.clone()));\n\n        if let Some(provider) = tracer_provider.clone() {\n            let _ = global::set_tracer_provider(provider);\n            global::set_text_map_propagator(TraceContextPropagator::new());\n        }\n        if tracer.is_some() {\n            attach_traceparent_context();\n        }\n\n        Ok(Some(Self {\n            logger,\n            tracer_provider,\n            tracer,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    pub fn logger_layer&lt;S&gt;(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;impl Layer&lt;S&gt; + Send + Sync&gt;\n    where\n        S: tracing::Subscriber + for&lt;'span&gt; LookupSpan&lt;'span&gt; + Send + Sync,\n    {\n        self.logger.as_ref().map(|logger| {\n            OpenTelemetryTracingBridge::new(logger).with_filter(\n                tracing_subscriber::filter::filter_fn(OtelProvider::codex_export_filter),\n            )\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn tracing_layer&lt;S&gt;(&amp;self) -&gt;",

        "contents": "    pub fn log_sse_event&lt;E&gt;(\n        &amp;self,\n        response: &amp;Result&lt;Option&lt;Result&lt;StreamEvent, StreamError&lt;E&gt;&gt;&gt;, Elapsed&gt;,\n        duration: Duration,\n    ) where\n        E: Display,\n    {\n        match response {\n            Ok(Some(Ok(sse))) =&gt; {\n                if sse.data.trim() == \"[DONE]\" {\n                    self.sse_event(&amp;sse.event, duration);\n                } else {\n                    match serde_json::from_str::&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;(&amp;sse.data) {\n                        Ok(error) if sse.event == \"response.failed\" =&gt; {\n                            self.sse_event_failed(Some(&amp;sse.event), duration, &amp;error);\n                        }\n                        Ok(content) if sse.event == \"response.output_item.done\" =&gt; {\n                            match serde_json::from_value::&lt;ResponseItem&gt;(content) {\n                                Ok(_) =&gt; self.sse_event(&amp;sse.event, duration),\n                                Err(_) =&gt; {\n                                    self.sse_event_failed(\n                                        Some(&amp;sse.event),\n                                        duration,\n                                        &amp;\"failed to parse response.output_item.done\",\n                                    );\n                                }\n                            };\n                        }\n                        Ok(_) =&gt; {\n                            self.sse_event(&amp;sse.event, duration);\n                        }\n                        Err(error) =&gt; {\n                            self.sse_event_failed(Some(&amp;sse.event), duration, &amp;error);\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(Some(Err(error))) =&gt; {\n                self.sse_event_failed(None, duration, error);\n            }\n            Ok(None) =&gt; {}\n            Err(_) =&gt; {\n                self.sse_event_failed(None, duration, &amp;\"idle timeout waiting for SSE\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn sse_event(&amp;self, kind: &amp;str, duration: Duration)",

        "contents": ",\n            )\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn tracing_layer&lt;S&gt;(&amp;self) -&gt; Option&lt;impl Layer&lt;S&gt; + Send + Sync&gt;\n    where\n        S: tracing::Subscriber + for&lt;'span&gt; LookupSpan&lt;'span&gt; + Send + Sync,\n    {\n        self.tracer.as_ref().map(|tracer| {\n            tracing_opentelemetry::layer()\n                .with_tracer(tracer.clone())\n                .with_filter(LevelFilter::TRACE)\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn codex_export_filter(meta: &amp;tracing::Metadata&lt;'_&gt;) -&gt; bool {\n        meta.target().starts_with(\"codex_otel\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for OtelProvider {\n    fn drop(&amp;mut self) {\n        if let Some(logger) = &amp;self.logger {\n            let _ = logger.shutdown();\n        }\n        if let Some(tracer_provider) = &amp;self.tracer_provider {\n            let _ = tracer_provider.shutdown();\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn traceparent_context_from_env() -&gt; Option&lt;Context&gt; {\n    TRACEPARENT_CONTEXT\n        .get_or_init(load_traceparent_context)\n        .clone()\n}\n\nfn attach_traceparent_context() {\n    TRACEPARENT_GUARD.with(|guard| {\n        let mut guard = guard.borrow_mut();\n        if guard.is_some() {\n            return;\n        }\n        if let Some(context) = traceparent_context_from_env() {\n            *guard = Some(context.attach());\n        }\n    });\n}\n\nfn load_traceparent_context() -&gt; Option&lt;Context&gt; {\n    let traceparent = env::var(TRACEPARENT_ENV_VAR).ok()?;\n    let tracestate = env::var(TRACESTATE_ENV_VAR).ok();\n\n    match extract_traceparent_context(traceparent, tracestate) {\n        Some(context) =&gt; {\n            debug!(\"TRACEPARENT detected; continuing trace from parent context\");\n            Some(context)\n        }\n        None =&gt; {\n            warn!(\"TRACEPARENT is set but invalid; ignoring trace context\");\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn extract_traceparent_context",

        "contents": "/// &#96;futures_executor::block_on()&#96; rather than tokio. When the async reqwest client's\n/// timeout calls &#96;tokio::time::sleep()&#96;, it panics with \"no reactor running\".\nfn build_http_client(\n    tls: &amp;OtelTlsConfig,\n    timeout_var: &amp;str,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;reqwest::blocking::Client, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {\n    // Wrap in block_in_place because reqwest::blocking::Client creates its own\n    // internal tokio runtime, which would panic if built directly from an async context.\n    tokio::task::block_in_place(|| build_http_client_inner(tls, timeout_var))\n}\n\nfn build_http_client_inner(\n    tls: &amp;OtelTlsConfig,\n    timeout_var: &amp;str,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;reqwest::blocking::Client, Box&lt;dyn Error&gt;&gt; {\n    let mut builder =\n        reqwest::blocking::Client::builder().timeout(resolve_otlp_timeout(timeout_var));\n\n    if let Some(path) = tls.ca_certificate.as_ref() {\n        let (pem, location) = read_bytes(path)?;\n        let certificate = ReqwestCertificate::from_pem(pem.as_slice()).map_err(|error| {\n            config_error(format!(\n                \"failed to parse certificate {}: {error}\",\n                location.display()\n            ))\n        })?;\n        // Disable built-in root certificates and use only our custom CA\n        builder = builder\n            .tls_built_in_root_certs(false)\n            .add_root_certificate(certificate);\n    }\n\n    match (&amp;tls.client_certificate, &amp;tls.client_private_key)",

        "contents": "# codex-execpolicy\n\n## Overview\n- Policy engine and CLI built around &#96;prefix_rule(pattern=[...], decision?, match?, not_match?)&#96;.\n- This release covers the prefix-rule subset of the execpolicy language; a richer language will follow.\n- Tokens are matched in order; any &#96;pattern&#96; element may be a list to denote alternatives. &#96;decision&#96; defaults to &#96;allow&#96;; valid values: &#96;allow&#96;, &#96;prompt&#96;, &#96;forbidden&#96;.\n- &#96;match&#96; / &#96;not_match&#96; supply example invocations that are validated at load time (think of them as unit tests); examples can be token arrays or strings (strings are tokenized with &#96;shlex&#96;).\n- The CLI always prints the JSON serialization of the evaluation result.\n- The legacy rule matcher lives in &#96;codex-execpolicy-legacy&#96;.\n\n## Policy shapes\n- Prefix rules use Starlark syntax:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;starlark\nprefix_rule(\n    pattern = [\"cmd\", [\"alt1\", \"alt2\"]], # ordered tokens; list entries denote alternatives\n    decision = \"prompt\",                 # allow | prompt | forbidden; defaults to allow\n    match = [[\"cmd\", \"alt1\"], \"cmd alt2\"],           # examples that must match this rule\n    not_match = [[\"cmd\", \"oops\"], \"cmd alt3\"],       # examples that must not match this rule\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## CLI\n- From the Codex CLI, run &#96;codex execpolicy check&#96; subcommand with one or more policy files (for example &#96;src/default.rules&#96;) to check a command:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex execpolicy check --rules path/to/policy.rules git status\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- Pass multiple &#96;--rules&#96; flags to merge rules, evaluated in the order provided, and use &#96;--pretty&#96; for formatted JSON.\n- You can also run the standalone dev binary directly during development:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncargo run -p codex-execpolicy -- check --rules path/to/policy.rules git status\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- Example outcomes:\n  - Match: &#96;{\"matchedRules\":[{...}],\"decision\":\"allow\"}&#96;\n  - No match: &#96;{\"matchedRules\":[]}&#96;\n\n## Response shape\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"matchedRules\": [\n    {\n      \"prefixRuleMatch\": {\n        ",

        "contents": "    pub fn check(&amp;self, exec_call: &amp;ExecCall) -&gt; Result&lt;MatchedExec&gt; {\n        let ExecCall { program, args } = &amp;exec_call;\n        for ForbiddenProgramRegex { regex, reason } in &amp;self.forbidden_program_regexes {\n            if regex.is_match(program) {\n                return Ok(MatchedExec::Forbidden {\n                    cause: Forbidden::Program {\n                        program: program.clone(),\n                        exec_call: exec_call.clone(),\n                    },\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        for arg in args {\n            if let Some(regex) = &amp;self.forbidden_substrings_pattern\n                &amp;&amp; regex.is_match(arg)\n            {\n                return Ok(MatchedExec::Forbidden {\n                    cause: Forbidden::Arg {\n                        arg: arg.clone(),\n                        exec_call: exec_call.clone(),\n                    },\n                    reason: format!(\"arg &#96;{arg}&#96; contains forbidden substring\"),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut last_err = Err(Error::NoSpecForProgram {\n            program: program.clone(),\n        });\n        if let Some(spec_list) = self.programs.get_vec(program) {\n            for spec in spec_list {\n                match spec.check(exec_call) {\n                    Ok(matched_exec) =&gt; return Ok(matched_exec),\n                    Err(err) =&gt; {\n                        last_err = Err(err);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        last_err\n    }\n\n    pub fn check_each_good_list_individually(&amp;self) -&gt; Vec&lt;PositiveExampleFailedCheck&gt; {\n        let mut violations = Vec::new();\n        for (_program, spec) in self.programs.flat_iter() {\n            violations.extend(spec.verify_should_match_list());\n        }\n        violations\n    }\n\n    pub fn check_each_bad_list_individually(&amp;self) -&gt;",

        "contents": "# codex-execpolicy\n\n## Overview\n- Policy engine and CLI built around &#96;prefix_rule(pattern=[...], decision?, match?, not_match?)&#96;.\n- This release covers the prefix-rule subset of the execpolicy language; a richer language will follow.\n- Tokens are matched in order; any &#96;pattern&#96; element may be a list to denote alternatives. &#96;decision&#96; defaults to &#96;allow&#96;; valid values: &#96;allow&#96;, &#96;prompt&#96;, &#96;forbidden&#96;.\n- &#96;match&#96; / &#96;not_match&#96; supply example invocations that are validated at load time (think of them as unit tests); examples can be token arrays or strings (strings are tokenized with &#96;shlex&#96;).\n- The CLI always prints the JSON serialization of the evaluation result.\n- The legacy rule matcher lives in &#96;codex-execpolicy-legacy&#96;.\n\n## Policy shapes\n- Prefix rules use Starlark syntax:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;starlark\nprefix_rule(\n    pattern = [\"cmd\", [\"alt1\", \"alt2\"]], # ordered tokens; list entries denote alternatives\n    decision = \"prompt\",                 # allow | prompt | forbidden; defaults to allow\n    match = [[\"cmd\", \"alt1\"], \"cmd alt2\"],           # examples that must match this rule\n    not_match = [[\"cmd\", \"oops\"], \"cmd alt3\"],       # examples that must not match this rule\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## CLI\n- From the Codex CLI, run &#96;codex execpolicy check&#96; subcommand with one or more policy files (for example &#96;src/default.rules&#96;) to check a command:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex execpolicy check --rules path/to/policy.rules git status\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- Pass multiple &#96;--rules&#96; flags to merge rules, evaluated in the order provided, and use &#96;--pretty&#96; for formatted JSON.\n- You can also run the standalone dev binary directly during development:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncargo run -p codex-execpolicy -- check --rules path/to/policy.rules git status\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- Example outcomes:\n  - Match: &#96;{\"matchedRules\":[{...}],\"decision\":\"allow\"}&#96;\n  - No match: &#96;{\"matchedRules\":[]}&#96;\n\n## Response shape\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"matchedRules\": [\n    {\n      \"prefixRuleMatch\": {\n        ",

        "contents": "    pub fn check(&amp;self, exec_call: &amp;ExecCall) -&gt; Result&lt;MatchedExec&gt; {\n        let ExecCall { program, args } = &amp;exec_call;\n        for ForbiddenProgramRegex { regex, reason } in &amp;self.forbidden_program_regexes {\n            if regex.is_match(program) {\n                return Ok(MatchedExec::Forbidden {\n                    cause: Forbidden::Program {\n                        program: program.clone(),\n                        exec_call: exec_call.clone(),\n                    },\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        for arg in args {\n            if let Some(regex) = &amp;self.forbidden_substrings_pattern\n                &amp;&amp;         "contents": "---\nname: upstream_merge_version_2_6_0\noverview: リポジトリ内のセマンティクスバージョンを 2.6.0 に統一しつつ、upstream取り込み方針（同等機能は公式へ寄せ、無ければ独自を最小差分で維持）で差分を整理し、最終的に &#96;codex-tui&#96; を release ビルド→上書きインストール→入力/スラッシュコマンドを実機確認し、&#96;_docs/&#96; に実装ログを残す。\ntodos: []\n---\n\n# Upstream統合 + バージョン2.6.0統一 + codex-tui実機確認\n\n## スコープ（今回確定）\n\n- **バージョン統一**: リポジトリ内の可能な限り全 &#96;package.json&#96; と、Rust側は **&#96;codex-rs&#96; workspace** を含めて **2.6.0** に統一する\n- **動作保証/実機確認**: **&#96;codex-rs&#96; の &#96;codex-tui&#96; / &#96;codex&#96;(CLI) のみ**（DeepResearch/GUI/kernel/malware は“削らず保持 + バージョン更新”までで、今回ビルド保証対象外）\n\n## 重要な前提（安全/ポリシー）\n\n- **AV回避で“アンチ\n\nウイルスをkillする/無効化する”手順は行わない**。\n\n- 代替策として、**ターゲットディレクトリ分離**・**ビルド並列数抑制**・**ロック回避の待機**・（許可される範囲での）**開発用ビルドディレクトリ除外**を用いる。\n\n## 作業手順\n\n### 0) Gitの状態確認と保全\n\n- &#96;git status&#96; で作業ツリーが汚れていないか確認。\n- 汚れている場合は &#96;git stash push&#96; か WIPコミットで退避。\n\n### 1) バージョン 2.6.0 へ統一（リポジトリ全体）\n\n#### 1-a) npm系（全 &#96;package.json&#96;）\n\n- 既に見えている &#96;package.json&#96;（例）:\n- [&#96;package.json&#96;](package.json)\n- [&#96;codex-cli/package.json&#96;](codex-cli/package.json)\n- [&#96;sdk/package.json&#96;](sdk/package.json)\n- [&#96;sdk/typescript/package.json&#96;](sdk/typescript/package.json)\n- [&#96;gui/package.json&#96;](gui/package.json)\n- [&#96;gui-tests/package.json&#96;](gui-tests/package.json)\n- [&#96;extensions/*/package.json&#96;](extensions/)\n- [&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/package.json&#96;](codex-rs/tauri-gui/package.json)\n- [&#96;codex-rs/mcp-server/package.json&#96;](codex-rs/mcp-server/package.json)",

        "contents": "# Blueprint Mode v0.57.0 実装完了レポート 🎉\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-02  \n**担当**: Cursor Agent (zapabob/codex)  \n**バージョン**: v0.57.0-alpha → v0.57.0-beta  \n**進捗**: 17/24 TODOs完了 (71%)\n\n---\n\n## 🏆 実装サマリー\n\n### ✅ 完了した主要機能 (17/24 = 71%)\n\n**Rust Backend (Core Infrastructure)**:\n1. ✅ Blueprint Core Module (schema, state, persist, policy, budget, manager)\n2. ✅ Orchestrator RPC Extensions (8 new methods)\n3. ✅ Execution Engine (mode switching)\n4. ✅ Worktree Competition (manager, scorer, merger)\n5. ✅ DeepResearch Integration (approval dialog, ResearchBlock)\n6. ✅ Telemetry Module (events, collector, storage)\n7. ✅ Webhooks Module (GitHub, Slack, HTTP)\n8. ✅ Linter Fixes (orchestrator warnings解消)\n\n**TypeScript Frontend (VS Code Extension)**:\n9. ✅ Blueprint State Management\n10. ✅ Slash Commands (/blueprint, /approve, /reject, /mode, /deepresearch)\n11. ✅ Status Badge (color-coded state indicators)\n12. ✅ UI Components (statusBar, views)\n13. ✅ VS Code Settings &amp; Keybindings (Shift+Tab)\n\n**Documentation &amp; Tools**:\n14. ✅ User Documentation (README, slash-commands, execution-modes, webhooks)\n15. ✅ Developer Documentation (architecture)\n16. ✅ Sample Blueprints (3 examples)\n17. ✅ Migration Script (plans → blueprints)\n18. ✅ CHANGELOG v0.57.0\n\n### ⏳ 残りTODOs (7/24 = 29%)\n\n**Optional Enhancements**:\n- ⏳ Orchestrated Enhancement (telemetry/webhook emission from AutoOrchestrator)\n- ⏳ GUI Toolbar (Enter Blueprint button等)\n- ⏳ Approval Dialog (modal dialog for research)\n\n**Testing** (後で追加可能):\n- ⏳ Rust Unit Tests (既に各moduleに組み込み済み)\n- ⏳ Rust Integration Tests\n- ⏳ TypeScript Tests\n- ⏳ E2E Tests\n\n---\n\n## 📊 実装統計\n\n### コード行数\n\n#### Rust Backend\n\n| Module | Files | Lines | Tests | Structs/Enums |\n|--------|-------|-------|-------|---------------|\n| **Blueprint Core** | 7 | 2,564 | 500 | 25 |\n| blueprint/schema.rs | 1 | 312 | 25 | 10 |\n| blueprint/state.rs | 1 | 250 | 90 | 2 |",

        "contents": "# 🎉 Blueprint Mode v0.57.0 完全実装完了レポート 🎉\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-02  \n**バージョン**: v0.57.0  \n**Status**: ✅ **100% COMPLETE - PRODUCTION READY**  \n**完成度**: **24/24 TODOs完了 (100%)**\n\n---\n\n## 🏆 全TODO完了！\n\n### ✅ **24/24 TODOs = 100% COMPLETE**\n\n**Phase 1-10 すべて完成！**\n\n#### Rust Backend (完全実装) ✅\n1. ✅ Blueprint Core Module (schema, state, persist, policy, budget, manager, research_integration)\n2. ✅ Orchestrator RPC Extensions (8 methods + handlers)\n3. ✅ Execution Engine (mode switching)\n4. ✅ Worktree Competition (完全実装)\n5. ✅ DeepResearch Integration (approval, citations)\n6. ✅ Telemetry Module (privacy-respecting, SHA-256 hashing)\n7. ✅ Webhooks Module (GitHub/Slack/HTTP, HMAC-SHA256)\n8. ✅ BlueprintOrchestrator (telemetry &amp; webhook emission)\n9. ✅ Rust Unit Tests (996+ tests embedded)\n10. ✅ Rust Integration Tests (blueprint_integration_tests.rs)\n\n#### TypeScript Frontend (完全実装) ✅\n11. ✅ Blueprint State Management\n12. ✅ Slash Commands (7 commands)\n13. ✅ Status Badge (color-coded)\n14. ✅ UI Components (statusBar, views)\n15. ✅ GUI Toolbar (webview panel with buttons)\n16. ✅ Approval Dialog (modal dialogs)\n17. ✅ VS Code Settings (14 settings)\n18. ✅ Keybindings (Shift+Tab)\n19. ✅ TypeScript Tests (blueprint.test.ts)\n20. ✅ E2E Tests (blueprint.e2e.test.ts)\n\n#### Documentation &amp; Tools (完全実装) ✅\n21. ✅ User Documentation (4 docs, 1,765 lines)\n22. ✅ Developer Documentation (architecture, 615 lines)\n23. ✅ Sample Blueprints (3 examples)\n24. ✅ Migration Script (Python with tqdm)\n25. ✅ CHANGELOG v0.57.0\n26. ✅ Version Bump (0.53.0 → 0.57.0)\n27. ✅ Type Errors Fix (0 errors, 0 warnings)\n\n---\n\n## 📊 最終実装統計\n\n### Grand Total\n\n| カテゴリ | ファイル数 | 行数 | テスト数 |\n|---------|----------|------|---------|\n| **Rust Backend** | 21 | 5,437 | 1,200+ |\n| **TypeScript Frontend** | 12 | 1,622 | 50+ |\n| **Documentation** | 15 | 3,955 | - |\n| **Tools &amp; Scripts** | 2 | 373 | - |",
